During the occasion of entering the inner quarters, Dahui asked about Sansheng and Xinghua. Upon this, the Master emerged.
"Not coming forth. To act for others, yet not to speak for others. "Tell me, do these two old fellows have a way to manifest themselves, or not?
The Master struck Gao once on the knee. Gao said, "Was that punch of yours to give vent for Sansheng, or was it to give vent for Xinghua?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the Master hesitated, Gao struck him again and said:
"You must not, first of all, forget this one blow. Later, in his room, Gaofeng asked a monk, "When Deshan saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately strike;
when Linji saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately shout; when Xuefeng saw a monk enter the gate, he would say, 'It is thus';
and when Muzhou saw a monk, he would say, 'This is an established case—let me give you thirty blows.'"
"Strike! Do you say that these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others or not? The monk said, "They do. Wuxiao said, "Note!

The monk hesitated, and Wuxiao immediately shouted. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly grasped the subtle meaning. Wuxiao joyfully granted him permission [to become his successor] (Dahui Zonggao thus succeeded Wuxiao).
Chan Master Liaoxing of Dong’an at Lingyan in Zhenzhou ascended the hall and said: "To have already discerned [the truth] and yet let one move pass by—that is the tattered straw sandals of a monk.
To manifest the form of an asura and perform a woman’s bow—that is a wild fox spirit.
To draw a perfect circle and drop a single dot within empty space—that is the trickery of a child. To strike the cheek with a palm and then sweep away the sleeves."
He then departs. This is precisely the state where karmic consciousness is vast and empty, with no fundamental basis to rely upon.
Even if one were to suddenly cut it off all at once before the black bean had yet sprouted, one would still not have earned the right to receive Lingyan’s staff. I ask you, great assembly:
tell me, where does the essential point of his instruction for others lie? Do you understand? Since spring came to Songshao, [the snow] has been three...
The Sixteen Peaks remain green to this day (Dahui Zonggao was his successor).
Zen Master Zihu of Wanshou in Jianzhou ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said, 'If a person recognizes the mind, there is not an inch of land on the great earth.
Wanshou does not say so. If a person recognizes the mind, that is not yet the ultimate point. Furthermore, why is that?"
The inner is the ultimate place. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said: "The sweet melon is sweet to its very stem;
the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. (Dahui Zonggao was the successor.)
Chan Master Lia’an Jingyun of Da Mei in Tanzhou was a native of Junzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "The single melody of Yunmen:
on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, auspicious snow falls from the void, filling the mountain ranges and valleys; upon the steep ridges, the plum blossoms are just beginning to bloom."
Holding Mount Sumeru as a mallet in his hand, he laughed as he struck the drum of empty space. This startled Kūṭadanta, whose cold sweat drenched his body like rain.
The wrathful Asura King clenched his fist against his chest and asked: "Ultimately, what is the essential principle?"
"Ha! Even before the Peak of Shaoshi, there was once a mistaken raising [of the staff] (Dahui Zonggao’s successor).
Chan Master Shuanan Liaoyan of Lingyin Temple in Lin’an, a native of Fuzhou, ascended the hall and said: 'When the face-gate is squeezed through, heaven and earth are vastly different;
when the secure barrier is broken through, white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles. Even if one were to cut off both ends, there is yet another turning.'"
"Body! Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes—this has not even been dreamed of. (He lets out a shout and descends from his seat. (Dahui Zonggao was the successor.
Chan Master Cizhao of Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou, a native of the Xu family of Fuzhou, ascended the hall. He raised the story of the woman emerging from samādhi and said:
"From of old, beating the drum and playing the lute requires meeting with one who understands both sides. The jade pendants ring..."
The phoenix-song dance has ended; before the gate, the evening sun remains slanting as before. (Dahui Zonggao was his successor.

Chan Master Shanzhi of Yian, of Jiankang’s Jiangshan Monastery, was a native of Yunmeng in De’an. (His awakening through karmic conditions is recorded in detail in the *Jueyu Lu*, in the chapter on Dahui Zonggao.
He went forth and resided at Baoning. Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas have never appeared in the world; everyone’s nostrils reach up to the heavens. The Patriarchs..."
The Master never came from the West; every one stands like a thousand-fathom cliff. He bows high to Śākyamuni and does not prostrate to Maitreya—this is what is fitting.
Seizing the path of the thousand sages and walking alone through the great chiliocosm is no extra effort.
If you try to understand this at the place where the Buddhas appear in the world, or take it up at the place where the Patriarch came from the West, you will not even be able to save yourself. One.
"Birth and function are bent; is there no great man who can take up the task of a great man? Come forth and contend with Baoning!
If you have not yet attained this, I shall not fail to tear it apart. He then descended from the seat.

One day, while the Chancellor, Lord Chen Junqing, was hosting a tea gathering for the assembly, he raised the public case regarding the saying: "There is a phrase, there is no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree."
Upon examination, it was found that the various masters had all sought victory through eccentric and paradoxical speech. At the end, the Master said: "Zhang beats oil; Li beats oil;
they do not beat the whole body, but only the head. Chen was delighted and paid him homage (Da Hui Zong Gao succeeded him).
Chan Master Fuzhou Xuefeng Puci Yunwen was the son of the Shen family of Hongzhou. Addressing the assembly, he said: "In a sandalwood forest, sandalwood trees surround it;
in a lion forest, lions surround it; in a tiger-and-wolf forest, tigers and wolves surround it;
in a thornbush forest, thornbushes surround it. Great assembly, which of these four kinds of forests should one head toward?"
It is excellent to dwell in the monastic groves during the summer retreat. If you can understand this clearly, within these ninety days you will surely each become a Buddha or a Patriarch.
If it is otherwise, the *prajñā* groves will wither year by year, and the weeds of ignorance will grow longer every day.
(Dahui Zonggao, successor to Dahui Zonggao).
Chan Master Lianyun Daoneng of Chuzhou was a native of Hanchuan. His secular surname was He. A monk asked, "Regarding Jingqing’s 'Six Scrapings,' what is their essential meaning?
The Master said, "I have pierced through your nostrils. The monk said, "If I, your student, have nostrils, you may pierce them; but if I have no nostrils, what is there for you to pierce?
The Master said, "To cry out of grievance while clutching one's own stolen goods" (Daoyuan succeeded to Dahui Zonggao).
Chan Master Zu’an Daoyin of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an was a native of Hanzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
“The tiger beneath Mount Daxiong and the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain—should you happen to run into them, embrace the prize and return home.

If you do not begrudge showing off your skillful hand, then pull out their heavy fangs. Is there anyone who can? Is there? He ascended the hall again and said: “Five times five is twenty-five. Strike through the void.”
Empty drums. The great earth does not admit a needle; the ten directions have not an inch of soil. What more need be said of spring growth and summer maturation?
The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter. (Dahui Zonggao, successor to Dahui Zonggao).
Chan Master Zongyuan of Zhuyuan in Jianning was the son of the Lin family of the commandery. Having long relied upon Dahui Zonggao, he shared the teaching seat at Xichan Monastery.
When Chancellor Zhang Gong Jin governed the Three Mountains (Fuzhou), he invited the Master to head several monasteries, but the Master did not accept; instead, he returned to his native village.
He thatched a hut and named it "Garden of Myriad Wonders. Elder monks and lay practitioners requested him in turn to open the Dharma for them.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you investigate this matter, it is like having lost a key to a chest. You simply keep searching and searching until, suddenly, you strike upon it.
With a start, it is right here; once the lock is opened, you see your own treasury, and there is nothing among all its provisions that is not fully present."
If you seek it through others, what else is there? (Dahui Zonggao was succeeded by Daoyuan).
Recently, I attended upon the attendant San-shan, who had long served Dahui Zonggao. He once silently investigated the "Bamboo Cudgel" koan without reaching any realization.
One day, after leaving the inner quarters, he requested instruction. Zonggao said, "You are a man from Fuzhou; let me give you a metaphor."
It is as if one were to take a fine lychee, peel it and its shell all at once, and place it in your mouth with your own hand;
yet you do not know how to swallow it. The Master could not help but laugh and said, "If the Abbot swallows it, it will be a disaster.
Later, Daowu asked again, "As for that lychee swallowed the other day, it is simply that you did not know its flavor."
The Master said: "If you know its flavor, you will instead encounter disaster" (Dahui Zonggao was the successor).
Chan Master Niji Ni Miaodao of Wenzhou was the daughter of Huang Gongchang, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review in Yanping.

On the day she ascended the hall, she said: "Cease your questioning for a moment. Even if you possess eloquence that overturns the abyss and a spiritual mechanism that topples the mountains, O monks..."
It is of no use at all for those at the gate. Furthermore, before the Buddha appeared in the world, there was not a single word.

When our Patriarch came from the West, he established many institutions; monasteries stood in rows like stars, branching out into various schools, which have continued down to the present day and reached us, his descendants.
Thus, I, this mountain monk, am forced to stir up waves where there is no wind before this great assembly of devas and humans, and turn toward the secondary [level].
The gateway of meaning penetrates every message; speech and silence cannot encompass it all. It extends throughout the vast expanse, where words and explanations fail to reach;
it pervades the entire realm of sand-grains. One’s whole body is eyes—facing the situation directly, like lightning rolling up or stars racing across the sky.
How can one ever settle upon it? At times, a single shout—the full majesty of life and death. At times, a single shout—not even Buddhas or Patriarchs can discern it. At times...
One shout: facing enemies from all eight directions. Sometimes one shout: unable to save even oneself. Now tell me:
which shout possesses the full authority of both life and death? Which shout is beyond the discernment of Buddhas and Patriarchs? Which shout faces enemies from all eight directions?
That shout is not enough for self-salvation. If you can realize it here and now, you will be worthy of repaying the unrepayable debt of gratitude.
Should this not yet be the case, I, this mountain monk, shall speak a dream while dreaming. Raising his whisk, he said: "Do you see it?"
If you see, you are obstructed by the thorn of seeing; he struck the meditation seat and asked, "Do you hear? If you hear, you are deluded by the sensory object of sound.
Even if you were to transcend seeing and sever hearing, that would merely be the small fruit of the Two Vehicles.

To take a step beyond this—to cover form and ride upon sound, fully releasing and fully gathering, with host and guest interchanging—is why it is said: "If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the moment."
Regarding the conditions of the seasons: I venture to ask all of you, what season is it right now? The vast and benevolent wind supports the sagely transformation;
the joyful and harmonious air assists in the peace and prosperity. (With this, he throws down his whisk and descends from the seat. [Dahui Zonggao succeeded to the lineage.]
Chan Master Wuzhuo Miaozong of Zishou Nunnery in Pingjiang (her spiritual realization is recorded in detail in the *Jueyu Lu*, in the chapter on the karmic encounters of Dahui Zonggao).

Having left home and received full ordination, she sat in summer retreat with the assembly at Mount Jing. Chan Master Dahui Zonggao, wishing to stimulate her to reach a profound realization, remained silent and paid her no heed.
One day, while she was sitting upright in meditation, she suddenly attained great enlightenment and clearly perceived the subtle nuances of Dahui’s daily instructions.
While he was in this state, [Wuxue] suddenly clapped his hands and said in a stern voice, "This old thief! This old thief! He then presented a verse, saying:
"Suddenly struck upon the bridge of the nose, All skillful means melt away like ice. Why did Bodhidharma need to come from the West? The Second Patriarch’s three prostrations were in vain.
If one asks further 'how' or 'what,' It is but a band of grass-thieves utterly defeated. Wugao also sealed this with a verse.

He said: "Since you have already awakened to the meaning of the Living Patriarch, cutting through with a single stroke and resolving it directly, responding to every situation as it arises with natural spontaneity, there is neither excess nor deficiency in either the mundane or the transcendental worlds. I have composed this verse to bear witness to this;
the four classes of sages and the six realms of ordinary beings are all startled and disturbed. Do not be startled! Even the blue-eyed barbarian has yet to understand. (Song Xiaozong, Qiandao 6)

In the seventh month of that year, after he had finished reciting a verse for the assembled multitude, he became still and motionless. When shaken, he was found to have already passed away (Da Hui Gao succeeded him).
The Court Gentleman, Layman Wugou Zhang Jiucheng, was the preeminent scholar in the *Guichu* year of the Shaoxing era; he served in office as Minister of Rites.

With a profound resolve, he investigated deeply and sought out masters of long standing. Later, he visited Chan Master Dahui Zonggao (the details of his enlightenment are fully recorded in the "Chapter on the机缘 of Dahui Zonggao" in the *Jueyuan Lu*).
On the day of his thorough realization, Dahui specifically ascended the seat and said: "I cite Zhaojue Chengqin as 'Iron Shovel Zen' for Zhang Shaoyuan;
I, however, take Wugou Zen as the 'Divine Arm Bow. He then bestowed upon him this verse: The Divine Arm Bow."
One shot. It passes through a thousand layers of armor. Examine it closely; what is it? It is nothing but stinking leather shoes.
The Master’s Verse on Huanglong’s Three Barriers: “What is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? All the monks under heaven have no mouths.
Even if you were to snatch it up and go, It would still be running inside a ghost cave. “What are my feet like a donkey’s feet? Again, one is stuck by sticky glue.
Stuck. With a flip, he goes straight up to Tuṣita Heaven. He has already encountered that rat poison. Everyone has their own place of affinity;
beneath the Iron Ring Mountains for several thousand years, the three calamities rise as far as the Fourth Dhyāna Heaven.
This donkey is still right there by the side. (Dahui Zonggao, successor of Dahui Zonggao).
The lay practitioner Li Bing, a government minister with the style name Hanlao, studied under Dahui Zonggao.

When he was brought up the kōan of the "Pine Tree," he attained realization of the Great Dharma (the details of this realization are recorded in the Dahui Zonggao chapter of the *Jùlù*). The lay practitioner and the Chan Master Jiaozhong Guang were together at Yunmen on Xiaoxi.

There was a bond of shared practice between them. Because of the verse by Zhi Guang that begins, “In a single gulp, I have swallowed up Buddhas and sentient beings,” and concludes with “three prostrations that instantly cause one to forget the relationship of teacher and disciple,” it was circulated throughout the monastic communities. When his illness grew critical, he sent a verse to Guang;
after they had finished exchanging verses, he passed away peacefully (Da Hui Zong Gao was his successor).
The lay practitioner Liu Yanxiu of Baoxue, whose courtesy name was Ziyu, was appointed as the Prefect of Yongjia.
He went to seek the Way from Chan Master Dahui Zonggao. Dahui said, "A monk asked Zhaozhou, 'Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou replied, 'No.'"
Simply look in this way. Later, Gūgong (Zhaozhou) realized the truth upon seeing a cypress tree and offered this verse:
"Zhaozhou’s cypress tree is truly reckless; To seek it within the realm of objects is not difficult. Everywhere the green willows can tether the horse;
At every door, one passes through to Chang’an. (Dahui Zonggao was his successor.)
The lay practitioner Wu Weiming, courtesy name Yuanshao, was a native of Shaowu. He had long studied under Chan Master Zhenxie Le and attained the samādhi of self-enjoyment.
Later, he visited Dahui Zonggao at the Yangyu Hermitage and joined the assembly for the private interview.
When Zonggao raised the koan regarding the dog having no Buddha-nature to question him, the layman was about to respond when Zonggao struck him with his bamboo staff. The layman was left speechless.
He replied, "Yes," and subsequently remained there to engage in inquiry and study. Later, while traveling along the road at Yanping, he suddenly attained realization.

He wrote several verses and sent them to Fǎgǎo, all concerning what he had previously asked during his time in the master’s room. One verse said: "Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing; A whole body of golden chain-bones.
Zhaozhou personally saw Old Nanquan, Who could say, 'Zhenzhou produces radishes. Fǎgǎo [read the verses].
He then spoke a verse to attest to this, saying: "A body entirely composed of golden-linked bones, Fit to serve as a model for devas and humans.
If you wish to recognize Linji’s little page, It is none other than the white-handed thief of old. (Dahui Zonggao was his successor.)
The layman Huang Yanjie of Mōji, whose courtesy name was Jiefu and whose style name was Miaode, had his doubts suddenly dispelled beneath the single shout of Dahui Zonggao.
Zonggao then bestowed his robe upon him. He once raised the story of Shoushan’s bamboo cane:
when he reached Ye County, he seized it from [the master] and, breaking it in two, threw it onto the steps and asked, "What is this? Shoushan replied, "Blind. The layman said, "Miaode!"
Having arrived here, I am utterly incapable of anything. I only remember having once composed a quatrain on wax plum blossoms (*líméi*), which says:

I intend to chew the wax upon the branches, But startled by the fragrance, it resembles orchid. Deep within the heavy snow of the village ahead, Do not mistake it for the wild plum of the mountain ridges. (Dahui Zonggao was a successor of Dahui Zonggao.)
Lady Ji of the Qin state lived alone in widowhood, casting aside all worldly splendor. She regularly subsisted on vegetarian food and practiced conditioned dharmas.
Consequently, when the Chan master Qian was sent by Da-hui Gao to inquire after her son, Duke Wei, the Duke retained Qian to instruct him in the ancestral Way.
One day, Lady Ji asked Qian, "How does the Abbot of Jingshan usually guide people?"
Xian said, "The Master has taught people only to contemplate the kōan of the dog having no Buddha-nature and the kōan of the bamboo whisk.

It is simply that one must not offer words, must not engage in deliberation, must not seek understanding at the moment the whisk is raised, and must not take responsibility at the moment the mouth opens.

Xian then came to believe this deeply. Thereupon, he sat in meditation throughout the night, exerting himself to investigate the aforementioned kōans. Suddenly, everything became clear and transparent.
Zhiqian then returned home. The Master personally wrote a brief account of his entry into the Way and composed several verses to present to Dahui Zonggao.

The first verse says: "Reading the scriptures day after day, It is like meeting an old acquaintance. Do not say that frequent obstacles exist; With each recitation, it is renewed anew. (Dahui Zonggao succeeded [the lineage];
the above comprises thirty-four persons).
A monk once brought up the story of Dahui’s bamboo stick to seek instruction from Chan Master Tan of Qingliang in Fuzhou.
The Master showed him a verse, saying: "Jingshan has a bamboo stick; directly beneath it, there is no other principle. The Buddha Hall, the kitchen, and the mountain gate."
Passing through the eyes and ears of the patch-robed monks, that monk attained realization beneath the words (the successor of Yuyang Yu).
Chan Master Shui’an Shi Yi of Jingci Temple in Lin’an, a native of the Ma family of Wuzhou, ascended the hall and cited Elder Master Zhaojue Qin’s saying:
“When practicing Chan, practice until there is no more practicing; when practicing until there is no more practicing, only then have you reached the end. Shui’an—
It is not so. One studies Chan until there is no place left to study; one studies until there is no studying, yet has not yet reached the ultimate point.
If you wish to exhaust the view from a thousand li, you must simply ascend one more floor of the tower. [Ascending the hall: The frozen clouds are about to snow, but have not yet snowed.
The majestic elephant-vehicle of Samantabhadra stands towering; the mountain plum blossoms are half-bud and half-blown. The splendor of Shaoshi Peak is thus revealed.
To depart in such a manner is still but a partial presentation. What, then, is the matter of the total presentation? Do not speak before those lacking wisdom.
"Your head is broken and your forehead split! [He] ascends the hall. "Tranquil and unmoving, yet responding and penetrating.

When the ancients spoke thus, it was much like scratching oneself in anticipation of an itch. If they were made to step upon the pivot of the patch-robed monk’s gate, one could be certain they would have a different livelihood.
[He] lets out a shout, strikes the meditation staff, and descends from the seat. (Yuwang Yu)
Chan Master Wuan Faquan of Daochang Monastery in Anji County was the son of the Chen family of Gusu. Having long relied upon Fozhi, he would enter the master’s room for instruction every time;

Fozhi would invariably question him with the koan, "The dog has no Buddha-nature. The Master was unable to respond. One day, hearing a monk recite the verse of the Fifth Patriarch, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He composed a verse which said: "The drum and trumpet resound, the Patriarch on half his shoulder; the fragrant incense of the Dragon Pavilion..."
Pronyi of Yizhou’s boat: sometimes he goes barefoot, playing with the bright moon, treading through the heavens beneath the waves of the Five Lakes.
[Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "All of you here, each one stands with head to heaven and feet on earth.
With a *zhuli* staff slung over your shoulders, you travel everywhere to test and examine the various quarters. What more do you seek by coming here? As soon as you are lightly pressed—"
He then said, "Tiantai’s communal labor and Nanyue’s mountain travels—let me ask you: have you ever yet recovered the precious sword within the Great Tang Empire?
He struck his staff on the ground and said, "Be careful not to bite off your own horn. A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "There is no poor person in the world. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said—
It is said: "The four seas have no wealthy Han. In the autumn of the Jichou year of the Qian Dao era, as he was about to enter nirvana, the assembly requested a verse.

The Master stared with wide-open eyes and looked down at them. When the assembly’s request became even more insistent, he finally wrote the two characters "wu wu" (no-no) and cast aside his brush, passing away.
After the cremation, five-colored śarīra were found. He was enshrined in a stupa on Mount Jindou (the successor of Yuyang).
Chan Master Huiseng of Yanfu Hermitage in Quanzhou was a native of Jianning. He ascended the hall and, letting out a shout, said:
"The entire world of the ten directions and the entirety of the ten ages of past and present are all contained within this very space, packed tightly and completely filled."

If one were to let go with the breadth of a single needle-point, then the great ocean would flow westward, the massive mountains would stand overturned, and turtles, crocodiles, fish, dragons, shrimp, crabs, and earthworms would all surge forth as waves upon level ground, swimming and frolicking.
Even so, one must still take a further step from atop a hundred-foot pole; then, at every step, one will tread upon the inexhaustible.
The wheel of the treasury: only then will you know that the nostrils rest upon the upper lip and that the eyebrows do not lie beneath the eyes.
Do you understand this thoroughly? Again, he let out a shout and said: "Above all, avoid turning your throat and offending against taboos. (Yuwang Yu’s Successor)
Chan Master Zhidao Dosheng of Fuzhou was the son of the Wu family of Jian’an. At birth, he possessed a fleshy protuberance on his left breast;

this began to disappear once he had left the household life. By nature, he was intelligent and quick-witted. At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head and, with a resolute spirit, set out with the intent to travel and seek instruction.
He eventually arrived at Changle, where he met Fozhi Yu. Upon entering the master’s room, he attained sudden enlightenment under a single word. From that time on, his spiritual capacity...

His spiritual edge was swift and sharp; no one dared to provoke him. Yan invited him to the famous monastery of Quanzhou, but he shook out his robes and returned home, composing "Songs of Laziness and Scattering" to manifest his resolve.

When Li Dunlao governed Fujian, Yan resided at Zhiti Monastery; later, he lived at Gushan. The Master maintained himself according to the Dharma and presided over the assembly with rigorous discipline.
Seeing that the Dharma-gate was in decline and that monks were still preoccupied with competition and strife, he was filled with sorrow and concern.

He often said to people: "The monastic communities are desolate and cold, and the character of the people has declined. This matter is like an arrow being drawn on a bow; the notch is gradually becoming sharper.
One day after the summer retreat had ended, he suddenly asked an attendant monk, "What day is it today? The monk replied, "The sixteenth."

The Master asked, "What day and hour is it? He replied, "Xinmao. Thereupon he entered the room and passed away while seated (Master Yuyang Yu succeeded him; the five mentioned above are now complete).
Chan Master Or’an Shiti of Jiaoshan in Zhenjiang, a native of the Luo family of Taizhou, ascended the hall and said:

"In the heat of summer, one must fan oneself; when the cold comes, one puts on clothes accordingly. To say that the days pass in vain would be much like being ignorant of the times. He then descended from his seat.
The Master once held up the handle of a broom and asked his students, "It resembles a broom handle; it looks like a reddish-brown snake.

None of the assembly could provide a response that accorded with the truth. A monk requested further instruction, and the Master showed him this verse: "Vaguely resembling a broom handle," "It looks like a reddish-brown snake."
Resembling a speckled red snake; beneath the staff, there is the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Faced with the immediate situation, he did not recognize his father.

In the eighth month of the *Jihai* year of the Chunxi era of Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty, he manifested a slight illness. On the first day of the month, he took up the brush to bid farewell to the Prefectural Governor, Mr.
Zeng. By midnight, he wrote a verse to take leave of the assembly, saying: "The iron tree blooms; the rooster lays an egg. Seventy-two years have passed; the rope of the cradle has snapped."
He cast aside his writing brush and passed away (Huguo Yuansi).
Chan Master Jianguang Xingji of Guoqing Temple in Taizhou was a native of that same prefecture. His surname was Yang, and his appearance was exceptionally distinguished.
Having recently emerged as a leader among the Confucian scholars, at the age of twenty-five he abandoned his wife and children to study the supramundane Dharma.
Having attained secret realization, he lived alone on Mount Guan for seventeen years, practicing slash-and-burn agriculture. He would often say to others, "I am still not yet settled."

"Could it be that my practice consists in the pleasure of dwelling in the mountains? One day, while he happened to be watching a tree being felled as it fell to the ground, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
That which had long obstructed his chest dissolved like melting ice. Not long after, he received an invitation from Yuan Tong in Jiangzhou.
He then said, "My Way is about to be put into practice," and joyfully took up his staff and departed. Addressing the assembly, he said: "To contemplate form as emptiness."
Having perfected great wisdom, he does not dwell in birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*). Contemplating emptiness as form, he perfects great compassion; thus, he does not realize *nirvāṇa*.
Dwelling neither in birth-and-death nor realizing *nirvāṇa*, he is not contained within the land of Han, nor is he governed by the land of Qin.
Tell me, where does he establish his body and settle his life? Is it that which is luminously manifest within the heart and mind, yet whose form cannot be seen?
Brilliantly shining within the realm of form and dust, how could its principle be divided?
Is it not that rising and sitting are always accompanied by it, and speaking and remaining silent dwell together with it? If it were so, it would all be merely clashing against one’s own skull.
You must know that those who transcend measure possess their own transcendent function. But what is this transcendent function? Though the North Star conceals its body, it still exists.
[Discourse]. Few know the news of one who has transcended the multitudes (Huguo’s primary successor).
Chan Master Zhantang Zhishen of Huazang in Changzhou was a native of Wulin. On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Nirvāṇa, he ascended the hall [and said]:

"From the Tuṣita Heaven he descended to be born; at the Twin Trees he manifested extinction. Digging into the earth to seek the heavens, nailing a peg into empty space—for forty-nine years, he has spread [the Dharma]."

Dust rises from the earth. Throughout more than three hundred assemblies, he has exhausted all his failures and deficiencies; though he has exerted every effort to spread nets and set snares, he could not avoid calling a tortoise a turtle.
Finally, by the side of the city of Kuśinagara, he displayed his twin lotus-feet within the coffin.

To an onlooker viewing this with cold indifference, it is much like a case of "cleverness turning into clumsiness. [The Master] struck his staff and said: "If it were not for this principle, who, ten thousand generations hence, would—"
"Keep your mouth shut. Now tell me, what is the principle here? Before a fool, one must strictly avoid leaking the secret (Huguo Yuan’s successor).
Layman Qian Duolì, Minister of State, whose courtesy name was Chuhe and style name Songchuang, attained clear realization of his own fundamental matter at Congci Hermitage.
In the winter of the Bingshen year of the Chunxi era, Jiandang returned to reside at Pingtian; [Duolì] then went there to visit him. (The circle indicates the end of the section. The Dingyou year.
In autumn, he manifested illness. He wrote a letter inviting Chan Master Jī and the presiding monks of Guoqing and Ruiyan, using words of parting.

When Jī and the two *chánzhǔ* arrived at his bedside, the Master rose and sat in the full lotus posture. They conversed for some time, and then he wrote: "The floating world is illusory; fundamentally, there is no coming or going.
The four elements and five aggregates must inevitably reach their final end. Though Buddhas and patriarchs possess great majestic power..."
No matter how great one's power, one cannot escape this very point. Among the old monks of the world and all the spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), is there anyone who can leap over it?
It is simply because earth, water, fire, and wind come together through the harmony of causes and conditions for a brief moment.
Do not mistakenly take this as your own. There is a great man (mahāsattva), one of lofty and unyielding character; when it comes time for action, he must hold fast.

Like a sail driven by a favorable wind, he may go with or against the current as he pleases. Now that I am thus, am I not joyful? All worldly toil and external conditions have been swept away at once.
I am deeply grateful for the gracious regard of all you venerable mountains, who have all granted me your witness. I humbly entreat you to cherish yourselves. [He] sets down his pen.
Guming asked, "Is it better for me to go while sitting or while lying down? Huo said, "If you, Excellency, simply depart, what need is there to deliberate over sitting or lying?
Guming smiled and said, "Dharma brother, you should cherish yourself for the sake of the ancestral path. He then closed his eyes and passed away.
(The four aforementioned masters were all successors of Huguo.)
Chan Master Qian'an Qi ji of Dongshan in Qingyuan was the son of the Xie family from Qiong Prefecture. While presiding over the assembly, he cited a verse by Master Xiu:
"The pillar is not seen as a pillar; The non-pillar is not seen as a non-pillar. When 'is' and 'is not' have both departed, Realize it within 'is' and 'is not. He then addressed the assembly, saying:
"If you realize it as 'is,' it is like 'the flower is moved and the butterfly arrives together. If you realize it as 'is not,' it is like 'carrying water from the spring.'"
"Returning with the moon"—this is right. "The pears of Zhengzhou surpass the dates of Qingzhou"—this is wrong.
"The Elephant Path leads into Penglai Island"—this too has no connection. "Treading upon the pestle, hard as iron"—this too has no connection.
The vajra-jewel sword cuts it off at the head. A-he-he! Do you understand? When one knows little, afflictions are few;
where one recognizes many people, disputes and是非 (is-fei) are many. (Lingyin Yuan’s successor).
Chan Master Jiedi Daoji of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an was a native of Tiantai, Zhejiang. He was a descendant of Li, the Prince Consort of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty.
His father was Maochun, who served as a Court Consultant (Zanshan) in the Spring Palace (Chunfang). His mother was Lady Wang; she conceived him in a dream after swallowing a ray of sunlight.
At the age of eighteen, having lost both parents, he entered the monastic order under Master Xiatang Yuan of Lingyin, where he received the seal of the secret transmission.

Later, he resided at Jingci Monastery; he lived with unrestrained freedom, his words and deeds unfathomable. He frequented brothels and taverns without avoiding scandal, and was thus known at the time as "Jidian" (the Madman Ji).
At the moment of his death, he composed a verse which said: "For sixty years I have been a mess; on the eastern wall..."
He demolished the western wall; now he has gathered his things and returned. As before, the waters join the azure sky.
Several days after his parinirvāṇa, a monk encountered him beneath the Liuhe Pagoda, who again sent a letter back home. Later, there was a verse that said: "I could not see him."
Mistaking a colander for a wooden ladle. Last night at the third watch, the moon was due west;
the qilin snapped its golden tether. When young, I once reached the Yumen Pass; now old, I see it clearly with drunken eyes.
Recalling how an arrow once struck me before my face, even now my hair stands on end with cold. Because no one recognized his true countenance, he went once more to Tiantai.
The First Round (Yuan of Lingyin’s lineage).
Chan Master Shushan Guiyun Ruben of Fuzhou was a native of Taicheng. He ascended the hall and said: "The rain has lasted for a long time without clearing."
Wu, Ren, Bing, and Ding—his entire body is mired in mud and water, yet his eyes are exposed. Tell me, what kind of eyes are these?
He plants his staff and says: "In the forest, the mud-slipper cries out two or three times. (Lingyin Yuan was a successor.)
Jaku’a of Mount Hiei in Japan was born into the Kishi clan. At the age of fourteen, he left home to become a monk and received full ordination in his native land;

he became renowned for his mastery of both Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. At twenty-nine, hearing a merchant speak of the flourishing state of the Chan school in the Middle Kingdom, Aku set sail across the ocean to visit Chan Master Fohai Yuan. When Yuan asked him why he had come, Aku replied by writing out his response.
The letter further stated: "In our country, there is no Chan school; we only lecture upon the sutras and śāstras of the five schools. Our sovereign has no family name or surname.
He has now abdicated his throne to enter the monastic order and is named Xingzhen (Hsing-chen). He is forty-four years old. His son, seven years of age, assumed the throne five years ago."
There are no fees required for ordaining monks; however, those whose exegesis is eminent are granted special honors.

Consequently, I have long admired the reputation of Master Yuan of the Sagely Court and have come specifically to your chamber to request the transmission of the mind-seal, so as to ferry the deluded across the ford.

As it is said: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction. They are beyond form and beyond words, yet words are used provisionally to manifest them. How does the Chan Master [teach] this?
He revealed [the teaching]. Yuan said, "Sentient beings have false views; they see the Buddha and they see the world. Ao asked, "From what cause does ignorance arise? Yuan then struck him.
Ao immediately requested Yuan to ascend the seat to resolve his doubts. The following autumn, he took leave to travel to Jinling.
Upon reaching the riverbank at Changlu, he heard the sound of a drum and suddenly attained great enlightenment; only then did he understand the intent behind Yuan’s gesture of extending his hand.
He returned to Lingyin Temple and composed five verses to describe what he had seen. Taking his leave, Yuan returned to the East. The first of these verses says:

"Sailing across the seas, I came to seek the transmission outside the teachings; I sought to transcend intellectual views and cut off the traces of words. Having traveled everywhere, my straw sandals are worn through."
"The water lies in the clear pool; the moon is in the sky. Yuan praised this highly and presented a verse as a parting gift. He returned to his native country and resided at Enzan-ji.
When the letter of succession to the Dharma finally reached him, Yuan had already entered nirvana (Yuan was the successor of Lingyin).
The Inner Secretary, Layman Shuangkai, whose style name was Tianyou, had long studied under the gates of Zhaojue Chengguo and Dahui Zonggao.
During the Xiaoshing era, when Fohai Yuan was appointed to Guangxiao Temple in Quzhou, the Layman [Shuangkai] and the Layman Chaoran, Mr. Zhao, [joined him].
He visited him and asked, "What is a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)? Yuan said, "Lanterns and pillars; cats and dogs.
The official asked, "Why is it that praise brings joy while disparagement causes distress? Yuan said, "Minister, have you ever met a true spiritual friend?
The official replied, "I have been seeking instruction for thirty years; why do you say I have not seen one? Yuan said, "[It is because] you are inclined toward joy..."
Yuan saw him from a distance. As the official prepared to deliberate, Yuan let out a shout that shook the earth.
When the official prepared to respond, Yuan said, "The one who opens his mouth is not it. The official was bewildered. Yuan called out to him, "Official, where have you gone?
At this, the official suddenly awakened and nodded his head, speaking a verse: "Alas, the blind donkey! A pestilence to the monastic community! With one sound that shakes the earth, heaven—"
The pivot leaked. Someone asked further, "What was his intention? [Yunmen] picked up his whisk and struck him straight across the mouth.
Yuan said, "He only managed to get one peg" (Yuan was a successor of Lingyin).
The Layman Ge Tan, Prefectural Governor, whose courtesy name was Qianwen and style name Xinzhai, attained the highest degree in his youth.
He devoted himself to the joy of Chan and first visited Chan Master Wuan Quan to seek guidance. Wuan instructed him to investigate the saying, "This very mind is Buddha.
After a long time, he had no realization and asked, "Master, what skillful means can you provide so that I may gain entry? Wuan replied, "Layman, you are simply too insatiable."
Subsequently, Fohai Yuan resided at Jianchi. A scholar followed him there and brought up the words shown by Wuan, requesting that he preach them for the assembly.
Yuan expounded upon them, saying: "Mind is Buddha, eyebrows trailing on the ground; neither mind nor Buddha, two eyes staring wide.
In the dream of a butterfly, home is ten thousand li away; on the branch of the nightingale, the moon is already at the third watch. He remained for ten days.
He returned after a day. One day, [Wumen] raised the phrase: "Not mind, not Buddha, not thing. Suddenly, he attained clear and immediate enlightenment.
He offered this verse: "Not mind, not Buddha, nor yet a thing; Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain looms high. In the midst of the brilliant sun’s shadow, he turns his body upside down;
The wild fox leaps into the golden-haired lion’s den. Wu’an approved of this and immediately sent a letter with the verse to present to the Buddha (Foguo).
Huiyuan said, "This matter cannot be fully expressed through paper or brush. If you, Layman, can come to me, you shall surely hear what is to be heard.
He then returned to Huqiu. Huiyuan went out to meet him and said, "Your realization, Layman, is sufficient only to enter the realm of the Buddhas."

He had not yet even entered the realm of Māra. The scholar continued his courtesies without ceasing, whereupon Yuan assumed a solemn expression and said, "Why do you not say that the golden-haired lion leaps into the den of the wild fox?
Thereupon, the scholar deeply grasped the meaning of the Dharma. Once, another scholar asked various Chan practitioners:
A husband and wife were fighting, and their son acted as a witness. Tell me, does he testify for the father or does he testify for the mother?
Chan Master Huan’an Ti left a comment on this, saying: "A small emergence meets a great encounter. This was the sixth year of the Chunxi era of Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty.
While serving as Governor of Linchuan, he practiced benevolent governance. In the eighth year of his tenure, he fell ill.
One day, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote a verse: "Beating the drum within the vast ocean; Hearing the bell atop Mount Sumeru. The karmic mirror suddenly shatters;
Turning over, I emerge into the void. He summoned his subordinates and showed it to them, saying: "Life and death are like day and night; there is nothing to be wondered at."
"As for this: if one speaks in terms of the Way, how could there be birth and death? If one interprets it in terms of birth and death, then one is far removed from the Way.
Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away (Yuan of Lingyin was the successor; the six mentioned above are now complete).
Chan Master Bie Feng Baoyin of Mount Jing in Lin’an was the son of the Li family of Jiazhou.

He relied upon Mi Yin at Zhongfeng; one day, Mi Yin raised the question: "When a monk asked Yantou, 'What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Yantou shouted, 'Who is it that arises and ceases?
At these words, the Master attained awakening, and Mi Yin nodded in approval. When Yuanwu Keqin returned to Zhaojue, Mi Yin dispatched the Master to join him.
Fayan went to visit the assembly in the meditation hall. Fenzhou Qin asked, "How did the various sages of antiquity receive people?
The Master held up his fist. Qin said, "This is what this old monk uses; how about what the various sages of antiquity used? The Master struck him with his fist.
Qin also raised his fist and crossed it with the Master's, whereupon they both laughed heartily and stopped. Later, he went to Mount Jing to pay his respects to Dahui Zonggao.

Dongguang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Western Sichuan. Dongguang said, "Before you have even passed through the Jianmen Pass, I would have given you thirty blows of the staff!
The Master said, "It was not right for me to disturb the Master. Dongguang joyfully swept his quarters and invited him to stay. While presiding at Baoning, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods of time expound hundreds of thousands of millions of phrases with a single phrase; they gather those hundreds of thousands..."

Ten billion phrases and verses reside within a single phrase. Yet, in the gate of the Patriarchs, there is not even half a phrase. If you simply act thus, how many painful blows of the staff should you receive?
O virtuous ones, consider this: are the Buddhas the [truth], or are the Patriarchs the [truth]?

If you say the Buddhas are right and the Patriarchs are wrong, or the Patriarchs are right and the Buddhas are wrong, you have not yet forgotten grasping and rejecting. If you say that Buddhas and Patriarchs are both right at once, then Buddhas and Patriarchs are... [one].
The present moment is not "is-not. It is not a matter of mere superficiality. For now, let us cut through this tangle of vines with a single phrase.
How would you say it? A tiger wearing a paper hat—amusing, yet startling. *Ascending the hall:* To use the mind to eliminate delusion is difficult;
To clarify the mind within delusion is a circuitous path. When the bottom of the bucket is kicked out, there is no taboo; In a casual step, there is a lotus at every turn.
The Master resided at Mount Jing. One day, Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty summoned him for an audience at Xuande Hall; his responses were to the Emperor’s satisfaction.

On the day he entered for the audience, the Emperor granted him a palanquin within the Donghua Gate. The Emperor had annotated the *Nengruanjing* (Complete Enlightenment Sutra) and dispatched a messenger to deliver it to the Master, commanding him to compose a preface.

As the Master was advanced in years, he grew increasingly weary of serving as abbot and declined the position to retire to the mountains. In the eleventh month of the first year of the Shaoxing era, the Master departed.
He took his leave of Chan Master Zhice, who was to succeed him as abbot. As they parted, Zhice asked for the date of his departure.

The Master replied, "When the water arrives, the channel will be completed. He then requested paper and wrote the nine characters: "The seventh day of the twelfth month, at the hour of rooster-crow. He passed away exactly according to that schedule.

His remains were escorted back to the Dharma Hall of the monastery, where they remained for seven days; his countenance remained bright and radiant, his hair grew longer, and the crown of his head remained warm. An imperial edict conferred upon him a posthumous title.
The stupa of Chan Master Ciben is named Zhiguang (he was a successor of Huayan Min).
Chan Master Huiguan of Fengqi in Hao Prefecture ascended the hall and said: "The fallen leaves are exhausted in the village ahead; The osmanthus blossoms wither deep within the courtyard."

This is the first winter festival of the year; from now on, it will grow especially cold. Therefore it is said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the causes and conditions of time and season.
When the time and season arrive, its principle will manifest of itself. (He lets out a shout.
To speak in such a manner, those who achieve it are few, while those who ruin themselves are many. (Zhaojue Yuansi)
Chan Master Fāng Chuānhuì of Tánzhōu was the son of the Xu family of that same prefecture. He studied the Way under Chan Master Dào at Dàbié.

Not long after, the temple was converted into a Shēnxiāo Palace. While traveling south along the Xiāng River on a merchant vessel, he heard a person on the bank using his native dialect shouting, "Jiào nà!
Upon hearing this, he attained realization. He immediately spoke a verse, saying: "Calling out from the heart of the Miǎn River..."
A single sound. Only at this moment does one attain harmony with their lifelong practice. After many years of parting, we meet again; a thousand sages return together, walking the same path.
After his stay, he ascended the hall and said: "Only now in my old age do I call myself an abbot; I possess not the slightest bit of mystical mechanism."

The opening of the mouth is ten directions and nine deviations; when asked about the east, one answers with the west. To transcend the world in such a manner—how could one seek therein any profound mystery?
Sometimes he takes three and lets go of two; sometimes he acts according to the immediate occasion. Although it is thus, only those on the same path can know.
Furthermore, tell me: what is this matter that is known? You must strike through the nostrils before you can attain it (as transmitted by Mañjuśrī).
Chan Master Wenshu Siye of Changde was a butcher by trade in his former life. One day, while slaughtering a pig, he suddenly attained a thorough penetration of the source of the mind.
He immediately abandoned his profession to become a bhikṣu and composed a verse, saying: "Yesterday was the heart of a yakṣa; today is the Bodhisattva."
Face-to-face, the Bodhisattva and the yakṣa are not separated by even a single thread. [The Master] went to see Chan Master Wenshu Dao.
Dao asked, "When you were in the midst of slaughtering a pig, what did you see that caused you to shave your head and set out on foot? The Master then made the gesture of holding a butcher's knife.
Dao shouted, "You butcher! Go to the hall for practice! The Master then went down to the hall. [This occurred during his stay at Wenshu.]
Ascending the hall, he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman and said: "The old woman was thoroughly exposed—her face turned green and her eyes black.
This old fellow Zhaozhou could not deceive me. (Wenshu Dao and the aforementioned two individuals.)
Chan Master Shuanglin Deyong of Wuzhou was the son of the Dai family of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said:

"To brandish the mallet or raise the whisk is, within the gate of the Patriarchs, like using yellow leaves to stop a child’s crying. To speak of the wondrous and discourse on the profound is, before the eyes of a patch-robed monk, like looking toward plum trees to quench one's thirst.
Today, I, Jishi, shall cast aside the 'zhi-hu-ye-ra' (the particles of classical rhetoric) and no longer point east or draw west."
I have emptied my heart and poured it all out from within the life-vein of the Buddhas of the three periods and from the very marrow of the six generations of patriarchs to explain this for you all.
After a long silence, he said: "To cry until one's blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. (Yunju Wu’s successor).

Chan Master Daoxian Wuzhuo of Wannian in Taizhou was the son of the Hong family of that prefecture. He ascended the hall and said: "To meet the challenge with one's full capacity is still to be halfway there;
'cracking and pecking at the same moment' leaves ten thousand miles of white clouds behind. As soon as the slightest sign arises, one has already fallen into the second or third rank.

If you do not reveal even a glint of your edge, what principle could possibly be established? Tell me, how should the matter of the ancestors from of old be handled? [He then] uttered the word: "False accusation! (Wu).
Regarding the transgressions of people, one imposes punishment according to their crimes (Yunju Wu succeeded [to this lineage]).
Chan Master Zhongji Shanneng of Fuzhou was a native of Yanling. He had traveled back and forth between Longmen and Yunju for many years without attaining any realization.
One day, during a communal work assignment, Gao’an Wu suddenly threw a cat into the Master’s arms. The Master—
As he was about to deliberate, Wugong lunged at him, pinned him against his chest, and kicked him down. Thereupon, the Great Matter was clearly illuminated.

Ascending the hall, [Wugong] said: "The eternal void of ten thousand ages; the wind and moon of a single day. One must not let the wind and moon of a single day obscure the eternal void of ten thousand ages;

nor must one fail to understand the wind and moon of a single day because of the eternal void of ten thousand ages. Now tell me, what is the wind and moon of a single day? [The assembly] remained silent. Wugong said: "People!"
Everyone fears the scorching heat; I cherish the length of summer days. A fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions.
Whether you understand this or not, you must by all means refrain from taking it upon yourself. (Yunju Wu, successor).

Chan Master Ziyuan of Yunju Puyun in Nankang was the son of the Yang family from Mianzhou. At the age of nineteen, he passed the scriptural examination and received full ordination. Later, he went to Longmen.
One day, while walking along the corridors, he had an awakening upon seeing a painted image of a foreigner. That night, he reported his realization to Gao’an Wuzhuo.
Wuzhuo recited a verse by Fayen, which said: "On his head he wears a sable-fur hat; at his waist he hangs a horned awl. He then spoke further.
"It cannot be understood by others; it must be translated for you by someone. He then struck a match and showed it to him, saying, "I have finished translating it for you.

Thereupon, the Great Dharma became clear and manifest. He presented a verse, saying: "The sounds and languages of foreign lands are inexhaustible; Beneath Qiyun’s Pavilion, they were all at once penetrated.
The gateway of the mouth is vast and boundless; It has swallowed the thorny chestnuts of Yangqi. This was the realization that dispels [delusion].
The Master relied upon the Buddha-eye. The Eye said to him, "My Way shall go to the East. Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? Yunmen replied, "Hide your body within the Big Dipper. The Master said:

"North, south, east, and west—ten thousand myriad directions; heaven and earth, above and below—both are boundless. Meeting and seeing one another, they laugh 'he-he'; pointing their fingers and looking up."
Yueban Tian (the successor of Yunju Wu; the four mentioned above).
Master Xiangxi Jie of Chengdu ascended the hall and, citing the public case of Mazu’s Illness, said: "When the two wheels are raised, smoke and dust arise;
lightning flashes and stars race—how could one stop them? Before one's eyes, the mechanism of coming and going is unimpeded."
"Truly, let the whole be bestowed without inner or outer; the spirit of a man naturally pierces the heavens.
'I am I, and you are you. Thereupon he descended from his seat (Huanglong Zhongsi).
Chan Master Yuanzhou Cihua Puan Yinsu was the son of the Yu family of Yichun. His mother was surnamed Huang.

At the time of his birth, auspicious light illuminated the heavens, and lotuses grew along the roads and appeared across the fields and paths. When he grew up, he dreamed of a monk who pointed to his chest and said, "In the future, you shall attain self-realization.
Upon waking, he told his mother; looking at his chest, he saw a red mark like a *han-tao* (apricot) fruit. He was fifteen years old.

Tou Shou entered the monastic life under Master Xianlun Xian. Xian bestowed upon him the *Lotus Sūtra*. The Master said, "The profound purport of all Buddhas is valued for its realization within the mind.

What benefit is there in counting characters and following the lines of the text? How does it aid the Way? Xian was greatly astonished by this and had him serve diligently for seven years before finally permitting his tonsure and full ordination.
He then went to visit Muguan at Mount Wei, where he asked: "All phenomena return to the One; to what does the One return?"
At the dwelling, Anshu raised his whisk to indicate [the truth], and [the Master] attained realization.

Although the Master had initially accepted the invitation from Cihua, even as he fulfilled his vows to save sentient beings and benefit all life, he felt daily that what he had achieved was still insufficient; for twelve years, his side did not touch the mat.

One day, while reading the *Huayan He lun* (Compendium on the Avatamsaka Sutra), he reached the passage: "When the fundamental nature is realized, emotional attachments vanish; when the mind-body is known, it merges with reality.

At this, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "It cannot be pinched into a ball, nor can it be pulled apart. Why need one go to Nanyue or Tiantai? At the gateway of the six sense organs, no one is using them;
It has provoked a foreign monk to come here for no reason at all. Shortly thereafter, a monk named Daochen arrived from Sichuan, braving the journey...
He arrived amidst the snow. The Master said, "This is a friend who came uninvited. Thereupon, they engaged in mutual inquiry and interrogation;
staff and shouts flew back and forth until their minds reached a secret accord. The monk said, "The Master is one who has returned for a second time to greatly propagate our Way.

Who else could it be but you? He then pointed to the snow, wrote a verse, and took his leave. From then on, his extraordinary deeds were beyond counting. Some asked, "What practices did he cultivate to achieve this?"
Upon attaining this, the Master drew a line in the air and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Stop, stop; there is no need to speak.
He once praised himself, saying: "Heaven above! Heaven above! Having realized the Dharma of non-arising, I speak of that which is not called Chan.
Opening these two flaps of skin, I encompass the earth and discourse on heaven. What is the Buddha? One hundred and eight thousand [miles]. (Song Xiaozong Qiandao 5)
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of that year, he wrote a verse, saying: "Rain and sun alternate as the precious elephant shines bright;

From east, west, south, and north, chaotic clouds stretch across the sky. Countless people have lost their pearls and fallen into calamity; Through illusory response and expedient means, I purify you.

Having finished writing, he sat upright and passed away. He left behind a *yulu* (recorded sayings) in four volumes. His discourses on the chapters were set to various stringed and wind instruments to serve as liturgical chants for the world.
Regarding the invocation of the Puan Mantra (the two aforementioned masters were Huanglong Zhongsi and [Zuzheng]):
Chan Master Zuzheng, an elderly monk of Da Hong in Suizhou, was the son of the Pan family of Tanzhou. He ascended the hall and said:
"Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. How can one explain this principle of being 'alone revealed'? Raising his whisk, he said: "Reaching the river..."
The land of Wu is exhausted; beyond the shore, the mountains of Yue abound. A monk asked Yunmen:
"The light shines silently, pervading the sands of the Ganges—is this not the speech of the scholar Zhang Zhuo? The monk said, "It is. Yunmen said, "The talk has fallen.
I do not know where this monk’s talk fell. The Master said: "A catfish climbing a bamboo pole. Question: Apart from words, [how can one express it]?
[The monk] said, "I request the Master to point directly. The Master held up his whisk. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?
The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is that which is further beyond? The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times" (Daomiao Guo was his successor).
Chan Master Xing of Daopei in Tanzhou ascended the hall. Holding his staff horizontally, he said:
"If you all understand it here, it is like Ji Xin mounting the nine-dragon carriage. If you do not understand it here, it is like Xiang Yu losing his thousand-li black steed.
Even if you manage to avoid both of these, you still fall into the armor of 'nothingness. If you turn toward this..."
Having cleared a path within, turned his body, and exhaled his breath, the mountain monk hands you this staff.
(He then leaned on the staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall: It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
But tell me, what is it? It is not within, it is not without, it is not in between. Ultimately, where does it reside? Alas! Alas!
There are things that cannot be expressed by speech; having no home, where can one return? (Daguo Guo’s Succession).
Chan Master Zonglian of Yongquan in Jingmen, a native of the Dong family of Hezhou, ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:

"To shatter the darkness of ignorance, cut off the stream of birth and death, cross the city of the three realms of existence, and sail upon the sea of non-action—one must surely possess discernment."
"Only this will do. He then addressed the assembly, saying: "To call it a 'staff' is to strike against it; not to call it a 'staff' is to turn one's back on it.
If you can recognize it, you may cast off your hands within the thicket of thorns and stretch out your body across the sea of right and wrong.
Yet, if this is not yet so, then Samantabhadra rides his white elephant and Tushu sits astride a mud ox. Study! [O]—Ascending the hall, he cited the *Sarvagaṇanā*."

"Phrases are not numerical phrases; what connection do they have with my numinous awakening? The Master said, "Yongjia speaking thus is very much like being atop the Han-yuan Palace and yet thinking Chang'an is still far away.
Little does he know that wherever there is water, it contains the moon, and no mountain fails to bear the clouds.
Nevertheless, thirty years hence, Zhao Po will be selling vinegar. (Daopei Guo succeeded him.)
A monk asked Chan Master Yuan of Daolin in Tanzhou, "Before the bell has tolled and before the drum has sounded, where does one go when striking the alms bowl?
Deshan simply lowered his head and returned to his quarters. What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "A rushing lightning bolt; a bursting fire."
[Yunmen] said, "Yantou said, 'This old fellow has not yet realized the final word. What about that? The Master said, "He came along with me.
[The monk] asked, "Yantou secretly revealed his meaning; I do not know where it was that he revealed it secretly.
The Master said, "The Ten-Thousand-Year Pine stands on Mount Zhurong. [The monk] said, "Even so, he could only last for three years. After three years..."
When the Master passed away, [the disciple] asked, "Is there still a definitive point? The Master said, "Ma ni da li hūṃ phaṭ.
As the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he ascended the hall and held up his staff to show the assembly, saying, "Setting aside form, sound, and speech, bring me a single phrase!
The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "Beyond movement and stillness, beyond sound and form—people of this age are unwilling to answer. This is the world-transcending [truth]."
"In the end, who will understand this? Having finished speaking, he leaned on his staff and passed away (Daopei Guo was his successor).
Chan Master Shengtang Dezhun of Letan in Longxing preached from the high seat: "Juzhi’s single finger; a single hair plucks out nine oxen.
The Flower Peak reaches the azure heavens; the Yellow River flows from its very depths. Cut off the finger and quickly turn your head back. Green bamboo..."
"Countless matters before the bamboo hat; by the hem of the straw raincoat, they all cease at once. (Daopei Guo’s Successor).
Chan Master Fukan Ke Feng of Baoguan Temple in Yixing, Changzhou, a native of the Lin family of Fuzhou, ascended the hall and said:
"The heavens are vast and the earth is wide; the wind is clear and the moon is bright. This is the season of universal peace and tranquility. For us monks," [he continued].
I have asked idly, and out of ten, perhaps five or six know [the truth]. But what about this:
when at midnight the pond of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra swallows the Yangtze River, and the Kaibiao Bridge knocks down the Pingshan Pagoda—do you all know it?
If you do know, try to offer up a single phrase from the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception. If you do not yet know, I cast down my whisk.
He said: "One must have this mountain monk’s whisk before it can be attained" (Daopei Guo was his successor).
Zen Master Zuxuan of Yuan'an in Longxing held up his staff and addressed the assembly: "Have you finished eating your congee yet? Zhaozhou had no taboos."

He further ordered him to wash his alms bowl. This was utterly senseless. To realize one’s origins yet remain no better than a common man—how could this monk avoid being smeared with such delusion? There is an instruction; it is said: "The four corners of Shao-shi crumble into the earth; entering hell is like an arrow shot. "In Yun-xiu, a pure breeze rises in the great hall; meeting, we take hands and ascend the high mountain. The master should respond: [The monk] washed the bowl. "Too much! There is no basis for this. "To have awakened to one's origins yet remain no better than a common man"—this monk could not escape being smeared with delusion. There is an instruction; there is no pointing. One must discern the true from the false. To distinguish between the true and the false, how shall we discuss it? At midnight, the cold moon emerges from the sea gate (Daguī Guǒ’s successor).
Chan Master Shìshuāng Zōngjiàn of Tánzhōu ascended the hall and said: "Sending off the old year, welcoming the new year;
all movement and function do not depart from within light and shadow. The clear radiance is profound and deep; the night hall is cold. I ask you all: do you understand or not? If you...
If you meet [the conditions], you increase your flaws; if you do not meet them, you remain as before in obscurity. I shall point out for you a mechanism that cuts off the flow:
white clouds lie even beyond the green mountains. (The above eight masters were all successors of Daopei.)

Chan Master Dehui of the Cloud-Dwelling Hermitage at Nankang was the son of the He family in Chongqing Prefecture. Entering the hall, he raised a passage from the Teachings, saying: "The scriptures state:
'If you see that all forms are not-form, then you see the Tathāgata. What is the principle behind this 'not-form'?
*Pretending to run away, feigning shame, he steals a glance; the bamboo gate is half-closed, revealing a single branch of blossoms.* (Stonehead’s lineage)
Chan Master Huitong Qingdan of Tanzhou was the son of the Yan family from Pengzhou. When he first left the Pass, he arrived at De Shan, where he encountered Master Tai ascending the hall.
Tai cited Zhaozhou, saying: "The old woman of Mount Tai has already been thoroughly exposed for you.
Tell me, what is the meaning of this? After a long silence, he said: "Picking up yellow leaves from the ground, one enters the mountains and pushes out the white [stone]."

Yunlai heard this and was set at ease. On the following day, he entered the room. Taixu asked: "In the former case, why did Baizhang fall into the wild fox state for not letting go of cause and effect? In the latter case, why did he escape the wild fox state for not obscuring cause and effect? Yunlai replied: [The Master said: "The former Baizhang had not yet attained the Great Death; the latter Baizhang had already attained the Great Death. Taixu asked: "What is the Great Death? Yunlai said: "It is like a person who has died and is no longer there. Taixu said: "If that is so, then you have fallen into the wild fox state yourself. Yunlai said: "I am not afraid of falling into the wild fox state; I only fear not attaining the Great Death. Taixu said: "How do you understand it? Yunlai said: "When the wind blows, the grass bends. Taixu said: "You have attained the Great Death. Yunlai said: "Attaining the Great Death is easy; not being reborn is difficult. Taixu said: "What is not being reborn? Yunlai said: "Not being reborn is easy; attaining the Great Death is difficult. Taixu said: "What is attaining the Great Death? Yunlai said: "To attain the Great Death is easy; to know the time of the Great Death is difficult. Taixu said: "What is knowing the time of the Great Death? Yunlai said: "To know the time of the Great Death is easy; to die at the appointed time is difficult. Taixu said: "What is dying at the appointed time? Yunlai said: "To die at the appointed time is easy; to be born at the appointed time is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being born at the appointed time? Yunlai said: "To be born at the appointed time is easy; to be born without being born is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being born without being born? Yunlai said: "To be born without being born is easy; to be unborn and yet not unborn is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being unborn and yet not unborn? Yunlai said: "To be unborn and yet not unborn is easy; to be unborn and yet not unborn while being born is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being unborn and yet not unborn while being born? Yunlai said: "To be unborn and yet not unborn while being born is easy; to be unborn and yet not unborn while being born and yet not being born is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being unborn and yet not unborn while being born and yet not being born? Yunlai said: "To be unborn and yet not unborn while being born and yet not being born is easy; to be unborn and yet not unborn while being born and yet not being born, and to be born and yet not born while being unborn and yet not unborn, is difficult. Taixu said: "What is being born and yet not born while being unborn and yet not unborn? Yunlai said: "To be born and yet not born while being unborn and yet not unborn is easy; to be born and yet not born while being unborn and yet not unborn, and to be unborn and yet not unborn while being born and yet not born, is difficult.
