The Way flourished ever more, and those who attained the Dharma were numerous. Suddenly, he retired to the Eastern Hermitage and manifested a slight illness.

He composed a handwritten letter to bid farewell to the various officials and nobles, and further offered two phrases to test those who had come to study, saying: "Why does a person of power and strength fail to lift their foot?
When the mouth opens, it is not upon the tongue. On the day of his passing, he addressed the assembly: "Those who have long gathered here are practitioners of the true path."
It is simply that the "Black Bean" method cannot be employed; it is difficult to shoulder the True Lineage.

The Buddha-dharma of Linji has reached its point of sinking into stillness. How painful, how painful! (Yunju Zhuang’s comment: “If the Great Ancestor Songyuan were to force the noble into the lowly by using the Black Bean method, what would be so extraordinary about it?

You must take the rope for binding the dead and pass it through the nostrils of all Buddhas and Patriarchs before you have any share of freedom. At that time, a monk asked, “Is the rope for binding the dead in the Master’s hand? Yunju said, “You blind fellow! He took up his staff and struck him).

He left a testament to his dharma heirs, Xiangshan Mu and Yunju Kai, entrusting them with the preciousness of the Great Dharma. He further wrote a verse, saying: "Coming, there is nowhere from which it comes;
going, there is nowhere to which it goes. In a sudden turn at the profound pivot, even Buddhas and Patriarchs are at a loss. He then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
Fanglong Lu You inscribed the stupa for Master Caoyuan Daosheng of Jianfu Temple in Raoyou (a successor of Tiantong Jie).
Master Daosheng was a native of Nanjian. He served as a seat-occupier at Yunju and later emerged in the world at Miaoguo.
He subsequently moved to Guifeng. Entering the hall, he said: "The rain and snow fall in profusion; water drips from the eaves. How excellent is this contemplation!"
"World-Honored One! You cannot leap out from within the grass; this is truly a great humiliation. A turtle at the bottom of the water drills through an iron wall. *Du!* [He] ascends the hall.
"At dawn, on the third month’s morning, the green peaks of Nanshan pierce the clouds. There is no need to seek further for the meaning of the Westward Journey;
outside the gate, the sound of the 'Pobingjiao' bird calls several times. [He] strikes his knee once and says: "A fine brother! [He] then chants the *Ling* (Numinous) verse.
The Rock Verses say: Clouds depart and clouds arrive, yet they have no intention; Clouds come and clouds go, likewise without mind.

When existence and non-existence are severed, where is the spirit? A solitary peak rises abruptly, its greenness reaching to this day. Later, while residing at Jianfu for over a month, he manifested illness (Tiantong Jie was his successor).
Chan Master Zuteng Zijing of Tiantong in Qingyuan was the son of the Gao family of Fuzhou.

He visited Miyun Yuanjie at Lingyin Monastery, where they reached a mutual accord like that of a needle meeting its eye; he subsequently received the master’s seal of approval. In the first year of the Baoping era (1225), by imperial decree, he ascended the hall at Lingyin and said:
"A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. When the tree falls, the vine withers. Where do the phrases return? Liang... [text ends]
Jiurui said: "I long remember the third month in Jiangnan; where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant.
Ascending the hall, he said: "First, dragging a stone; second, moving earth. At midnight, the sun is at its zenith. Old An once herded the oxen of Mt. Mui;
Nanquan did not beat the drum of Yanguan. I inform you all: do not be reckless. A cricket in the fire swallows a tiger!"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: Once, when a monk knocked on the door at Heilin, Heilin asked, "Who is it?
The monk replied, "A wandering monk. Heilin said, "Not only a wandering monk; even if a Buddha were to come here, he would not be admitted.
The monk asked, "Why would even a Buddha not be admitted? Heilin replied, "Because there is no place for him to dwell. The Master said: "At Tiantong, it is not so. If someone were to knock..."
The gate was opened wide. Waiting for him to enter, [the Master] grabbed him by the chest and said, "Speak! Speak!

Had he attempted to open his mouth, [the Master] would have struck him with a fist right through the breast. If one can turn one's body and breathe freely within this state, then you may be settled beneath the bright window toward the higher realm (Tiantong Jue was the successor).
Chan Master Qián'ān Huìguāng of Jìngcí Monastery in Lín'ān composed a verse on refining salt, which says: "Water and mud are boiled together in one place;
When the water dries and the mud is purified, snow-flakes of salt bloom. Seizing the moment to raise it up at a price that reaches the heavens— The official seal is clear;
who would dare dispute it? (Tiantong Jie was his successor).

Chan Master Wàn'ān Zhìróu of Tàipíng Yǐnjìng was the son of the Chén family of Cháozhōu; his mother was surnamed Huáng. When the Venerable Nányuán Mìxǐ was exiled southward, his path led through Cháozhōu.
The master’s grandfather, Xiān, received him with the utmost courtesy and reverence. The master’s mother dreamed of a monk entering her chamber, whereupon she became pregnant.
Upon his birth, his parents vowed not to bind him with the burdens of worldly life. He shaved his head, donned the dyed robes, and completed his ordination.
Mian Jie was at Jiangshan. One day, during a session in the inner quarters, Jie raised the topic: "Śākyamuni and Maitreya are still his servants; tell me, who is he?
The Master said, "A man with no place to stand. Jie said, "A thousand hearings are not equal to one seeing.
The Master then struck him once with his fist. Jie seized him and said in a stern voice, "You little devil! What have you seen?"
"Ma! Hu da-luan-da! The Master said, "Do you want another punch? Jie struck twice in succession and said, "The one who strikes has no place to stand.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and subsequently took his leave. (Fayin Kang’s verse says: "The fist lands everywhere in empty space;

where has this fellow ever lacked a place to stand? Four or five hundred lanes of flowers and willows; two or three thousand pavilions of pipes and strings. He went forth to reside at Tàipíng Yǐnjìng. Ascending the hall, he began his discourse.
To go from the Bodhi tree to the Deer Park is not the ultimate vehicle; to transmit the teachings of Shaoshi and continue the lineage of Caoqi is not yet to be considered a man of true character.
Only when one reaches the state of being without dependence and without desire, such that not a single dharma confronts the mind, does one still fall into the second view.

To let this matter pass is to have the power of rolling up and unfolding according to one’s own will, seizing or releasing as the occasion demands; to grant passage at the very point where one might hold fast, so that the lamp-stand and the lantern become alive.
"Vivacious! At the point where one lets go, one must hold fast. Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his servants. [He] strikes the meditation staff.

"Tell me, is this letting go, or is it holding fast? A single breath, silent, contains all forms; where can the myriad spirits fail to express their gratitude for His impartiality? [Ascending the hall:
Master Dongshan said, "The path to the Gate of Emptiness is reached by all who travel it; only those who have arrived truly know it."
"Knowing the ultimate intent is long-standing; in the mind-ground, no weeds grow. Naturally, the body emits white light from its brow.
The Master said, "Dongshan only knows how to seek existence within non-existence, but does not know how to seek non-existence within existence.

It is not so with Yijing: 'Those who reach the path through the gate of emptiness are all there; only those who have reached it know that where there is obstruction, there is penetration. Planting flowers upon a stone, they yet bear fruit.'"

In the end, it truly does not depend on the spring breeze. When the Master was approaching his death, he gathered the assembly and instructed them, saying, "This old monk has lived his life without any superfluous possessions;
it will suffice for me to rest in the Hall of Tranquil Sleep according to the usual custom of the community for two days.

He then wrote a verse and passed away while sitting upright. Three days later, the temple was destroyed by fire. The assembly realized that his final words were intentional. (Tiantong Jie was his successor.)
Chan Master Xia’an Liaowu of Lingyin in Lin’an was a native of Gusu. He ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where a monk asked Muzhou:
'I do not ask about proceeding from one layer to the next; what is it like when one does not proceed from one layer to the next?'"
The Master of the Province said: "Yesterday I planted eggplants; today I plant melons. The Verse says: Yesterday I planted eggplants; Today I plant melons.
A single note of the *Hemanzi* melody— With the moon, in whose house does it fall? (Tiantong Jie’s Succession)
Chan Master Qingru Yiweng of Mount Jiang in Jinling was surnamed Fan and was a native of Changle, Fuzhou.
He ascended the hall and said: "The spring rain is like rich cream; the spring clouds resemble cranes; the spring birds warble; the spring waters flow clear.
Lifting open the skull-cup of Avalokiteśvara and kicking over the pavilion of Maitreya—do not, by any means, compound error with error. He struck the meditation seat and said, "Study! (○)
Ascending the hall, [Tiantong Jue] said: "The Tathāgatas of the past have already accomplished this gate. One blind man leads a multitude of blind men.
The Bodhisattvas of the present each now enter perfect clarity. A shrimp leaps but cannot get out of its basket. Those who practice and study in the future should rely upon this Dharma;
otherwise, they will bring about the destruction of an entire ship. (Tiantong Jue was the successor.)
Chan Master Yunshao of Chengtian Temple in Pingjiang studied under Mian Huijie. After receiving his formal certification (*jibie*), he resided at Chengtian.
On the anniversary of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa, he ascended the hall and said: "When this old fellow was in the eighth month of the year, At the dead of night, my madness broke loose."
"Only just now did he drive in that long nail into his eyes; even until this day it has not been pulled out.
Today I, this mountain monk, shall employ a lethal hand to pull it out for him once and for all. Having said this, he descended from the seat. (Tiantong Jie’s Succession)
The scholar and lay practitioner Zhang Zi, whose courtesy name was Gongfu and alternative style name Yuezhai, attained awakening upon hearing the sound of a bell.
He composed a verse, saying: "A single strike of the bell, The faculty of hearing is blocked. From within this mass of flesh, the thief is driven out.
If someone asks what school I follow, The face of the Śūnyatā-deva is black. Later, he donated his residence to establish a temple named Huiyun and invited Pō’ān Xian to serve as its abbot.
The Chan Master founded this mountain. His inscription states: "To relinquish a forest dwelling for an *āraṇya*—how could this be a minor matter?

I entreat a patriarch to occupy the curved wooden seat (the Dharma throne) solely for the sake of the Great Matter. Having traveled extensively to seek instruction many times, I was struck by Miam until my nostrils were lost.

One morning, he brought it forth and stripped away my face-skin at Cold Spring. Had I not anticipated its fragrant excellence, why would I have troubled myself with such solemnity? I bid farewell to the green."

Pines stand by the northern ravine, piercing through several layers of clouds emerging from the peaks; facing the green waters of the southern lake, one prays for a ten-thousand-year lifespan as enduring as a mountain.
In the fifth year of the Jiading era, the Master restored the purity of the lineage and succeeded the Dharma Master Wenglun in propagating the Dharma.
Today, there is a dedicated shrine for him at Huiyun (the successor of Tiantong Jie). [The above comprises ten individuals.]
Chan Master Zheng’an Zongguang of Jingju Monastery at Qingyuan in Jizhou ascended the hall and said: "Do not cherish the holy; 'holy' is a provisional name.
Do not loathe the mundane; 'mundane' is a conceptual construct. Once the sentiments of holiness and mundanity are exhausted, subject and object naturally vanish together.
At such a time, who can truly comprehend it? The stone woman pierces the needle while the mountain colors remain exquisite; the wooden man pulls [the shuttle]..."
Xian Haiyun Sheng (Successor of Qingyuan Yi).
Chan Master Huiweng Wuming of Jingci Temple in Lin’an was a native of Fuzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "I cite a case where a monk from under the guidance of Jia Shan went to Gaoting.
As soon as he prostrated, Gaoting struck him. The monk said, 'I have come specifically to pay my respects; why do you strike me?'"
He bowed again. The attendant struck him and drove him out. The monk returned and reported this to Jiashan. Jiashan asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.
Jiashan said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. Had you understood, my mouth would have been closed for good. Ying'an Hua commented:
Gaoting was the first to find himself unable to restrain his laughter. Alas, how regrettable that he let the monk pass with his staff too hastily!
Had this monk been a true man at that time, let alone Gaoting or Jia Shan—even if Master Bodhidharma himself had appeared, he would have cut him into three pieces.
Why? "When the family is prosperous, filial sons are born; when the state is powerful, strategic ministers arise. The Master said, "Gaoting and Jia..."
The mountain gateways and courtyards are each arranged as is appropriate; it is only that one person in the middle is slightly lacking.

When Master Ying’an speaks thus, it is merely a tea-pot from Gong County. The Master once compiled and edited the *Lian Deng Hui Yao* (Essentials of the Linked Lamps), which has been transmitted throughout the monastic communities.

(Gushan Yongsi: [In] Shu, the lineage of Buddhas and Dao is priceless; it records Mingzhi’s successor as Kuku, Kuku’s successor as Fadu, Fadu’s successor as Cici, Cici’s successor as Yiyuan, Yiyuan’s successor as Xiaoyuan, and Xiaoyuan’s successor as Miaomi.)

Succeeding these two were Yangqin; Yangqin succeeded Wunian; Youyou succeeded Jingshan Baobao; Tie-niu succeeded Yuanyuan; Chaoyang succeeded [them], down to Juyun and all the other Dharma heirs, who continued the lineage of Dahui Zonggao after his line had been severed, greatly flourishing in the Jinjiang region.

I await the inclusion of their recorded sayings (*jiyu*) to supplement this account, for while the *Jiaxing Zhuzang* contains the records of the various masters of the "Restoration" period, it lacks the biographical facts of the masters of the "Bitter Words" period. The merit of Master Jideng is greatest; may those in all quarters not be sparing with their instruction.
Chan Master Zangcou Shanzen of Jingshan in Lin’an was the son of the Lü family of Nanan in Quanzhou. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"The ancients said, 'The single word "knowing" is the gateway to all wonders. Yet others said, 'The single word "knowing" is the gateway to all calamities.
Regarding these two gateways, once you have entered them, you must also be able to exit them. The Buddhas of the three periods could not exit them."
The six ancestral masters could not produce it; the old monks of the world could not produce it. Why? It is easy to transform iron into gold;
it is difficult to transform gold into iron. [The Master] occupies the room. Is this place where one comes after having made inquiries and burned incense, standing by the side of this old monk?
You fool! It would be tolerable enough if you were merely dull-witted yourself, but do not come here to be dull-witted as well.
The Old Monk [Zhaozhou] left behind this self-inscription on his portrait: "I have attained no enlightenment through Zen meditation; my literacy is limited to a few characters.
My eyes are triangular like those of a sorrowful foreigner from Mount Yan; my face is wrinkled like Zhao Po sipping vinegar.
In one stroke, I stand far above all others—dare I say that rice is made of grain? (Lingyin Shansi)
Chan Master Dongcou Zhongying of Jingci Temple in Lin’an ascended the hall and said: “Above all, do not seek it following others; there is no need to look for it within yourself.
Transverse and vertical, lively and agile—there is letting go and there is gathering in. What is this? When one leaf falls, the whole world turns autumn.
He ascended the hall again and said: “It is not above in heaven, nor below in earth, nor in between among men. He let out a shout.
Now tell me, where does this one shout land? If you can understand it, there is guest and there is host;
there is illumination and there is function. If you do not understand it, withdraw from the assembly, go on patrol, and eat your meal.
[Circle] Entering the hall: the attendants walk, the seated ones sit; left or right, there is nothing that is not permissible. Thorns in the garden of ambrosia. Yellow...
The honey-fruit atop the *gambhari* tree: it is just so, yet not just so; not just so, yet just so.
A skilled merchant does not allow his goods to stagnate. (Lingyin Shansi)
Chan Master Yunzong Miao of Longji in Jixian was the son of the Wang family of Luling. From childhood, he delighted in sitting in meditation. At the age of twelve, he left the household life;

at nineteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination. At twenty-two, he began traveling to visit various masters. His first stop was to pay homage to Miaofeng, whom he encountered on the anniversary of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa.
As Miaofeng ascended the hall, he held up his staff and said, "The Old Śākyamuni has arrived! Do you all see him?"
"Do you see? This subtle, wondrous, pure Dharma-body possesses the thirty-two marks. He then set down his staff and said, "I see that none of you understand;
go enter nirvana! At these words, the Master attained sudden and profound enlightenment.

He subsequently ascended Mount Foding on the eastern side of Jishui, where he found the old site of the mountain master Xiu. There he lived on wild fruits and drank from mountain streams, never venturing beyond the mountains.
He once composed this verse for himself: "The mountain monk has his lot dwelling in the misty thickets; No rice, no money—let him mind none of it.
The water is like lapis lazuli, the mountains like jade; Before my eyes, there is as much as this. Later, Houfeng sent him a Dharma robe, a bamboo staff, and a self-portrait he had inscribed, saying:
"Upon the solitary peak of Miaofeng, the grass grows lush and tall; I hold across my lap a bamboo staff three feet long."
"Only Iron. It is permitted only for the Buddha-peak [Linji] and Longji to know; father and son do not transmit the true secret instruction.

In the Dinghai year of the Zhiyuan era, he suddenly manifested illness. He gathered the assembly to entrust them with his final affairs. Tapping his fingers once, he said: "This alone is my parting word to the assembly."
The assembly requested verses, but the Master did not respond. When the second watch of the night was approaching, he again asked for a brush and wrote:

"A single lamp remains within sight; there is no further speech. The great earth sinks level; empty space shatters. Having finished writing, he passed away in stillness. (The above three were the dharma heirs of Lingyin.)
Chan Master Wuchu Daguan of Yuyang in Qingyuan was the son of the Lu family of Hengxi in Ning County.

He studied under Beijian at Jingci Monastery, where he attained realization of the fundamental principle. Beijian appointed him to oversee literary affairs. Later, he resided at Yuyang. Entering the hall for a discourse, he said: "One winter, two winters;
you and I, you and I—stealing smiles in the dark, deceiving right before our faces. Though this is but ordinary tea and rice, who knows the grain?"
“There are insects inside. A fine wind has come at night, blowing down a pine tree in front of the gate” (Beijian Jian Si).
Chan Master Yancui Guangwen of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Lin family of Houguan. At eighteen, he received the tonsure and the full precepts.
He studied under various elders of the lineage, including Tieniu Yin, Shaoshi Mu, and Wujie Pai. Later, he attended upon Zeweng Yan.
Tiantong said, "Though the needle and the mustard seed may meet, I know for myself that it is not yet secure. Later, when he visited Shuangjing again, Yan smiled and asked, "Have you come?
One night, while sitting on the eaves, he heard the watchman strike the gong three times; as he entered the hall, his sandals caught and he stumbled.

It was like waking from a dream. The following morning, he went to the master's quarters. When Yan brought up the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl, Tiantong was about to open his mouth when Yan—

He suddenly stopped him with his fist; at that moment, his doubts were instantly dissolved like ice melting. In the Wuzi year of the Shaoding era (1268), Duke Hu, the military governor of Siming, invited him to Xiao Jingci.
He subsequently resided at the mountains of Xiangshan, Wanshou, Xuedou, Yuwang, Jingci, Lingyin, and Jingwu.
On the occasion of opening the furnace, he ascended the hall and cited Zhaozhou’s instruction to the assembly, saying: "This old monk has three..."
Ten years ago, at the hearth in the south, there was a saying regarding the absence of host and guest that remains unraised by anyone to this day.
The Master said: "The myriad phenomena of the forest and mountains, brightness and darkness, form and emptiness—these are proclaimed day and night.

The Ancient Buddha Zhaozhou did not fail to know them; it was simply because he was too eager to reach his destination. [Ascending the hall: "Yangqi’s eyes are like the pupils in one's own eyes. When facing...

The marrow of the crown of Jì’s head: first, it is not accomplished; second, it is not so. When the point is reached, it does not come; white clouds stretch for ten thousand miles (Jìngshān Yǎn’s successor).
Chán Master Dàtǒng Pùjì of Língyǐn Monastery in Lín’ān, a native of Fènghuà in Míngzhōu, ascended the hall and raised the following case:
When a monk asked Elder Mùzhōu, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Mùzhōu said, “A troop of monks arrives.”

A group of patch-robed monks departs. The verse says: A group of patch-robed monks comes; A group of patch-robed monks goes. Having broken through Muzhou’s barrier, The great earth has not a single inch of soil.
*Inscription on the Image of the World-Honored One Leaving the Mountain:* Dragon-marked and phoenix-natured, he leaves the royal palace;
Sleeves bare and robes tattered, he descends the Snowy Peak. His wisdom-vow must empty all realms of existence; One knows not how many existences there are.
At that time, there was Master Xuankong (Jingshan Yan-si), who had previously compiled and edited the *Wudeng Huiyuan* for circulation.
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Huaihai from Jing Mountain in Lin’an was the son of the Pan family of Jinghai in Tongzhou.
At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination. He went to visit Zhejiang Weng Yan at Jing Mountain, where Yan asked him, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Huai."
Dongyan said, "The Great Sage of Sizhou—why did he appear in Yangzhou? The Master said, "Today he has run into him again in Hangzhou. Dongyan said, "I am glad there is no connection [between us].
The Master said, "I have come from afar to catch a glimpse of your wind. Because Dongyan was sharp and quick-witted, the Master wished to greatly stimulate him;
however, he did not permit him to enter the hall for formal study. As soon as Dongyan saw him, he said, "Give me a turning word."
As he was about to open his mouth, [Zhaozhou] shouted it out. The Master presented a letter and also offered a verse; the final line read:
"Emptying my teachings, I turn my head to gaze at Chang'an. Yan said, "What kind of place is this? The Master replied, "Thank you, Preceptor, for granting me lodging."

Thereupon, he was secretly admitted into the ranks of the inner quarters and appointed as the head of the Secretariat (Jishishi). After Yan entered nirvana, the throne at Yuyang Monastery in Siming remained vacant;
the imperial court petitioned for the Master to fill the position. He subsequently moved to Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou and then to Lingyin and Jingshan.

During his tenure at Jingshan, he encountered the aftermath of a famine, with unpaid debts piling up like mountains and the monks residing in dilapidated old buildings. Yet, before long, multi-storied pavilions rose high toward the heavens. Clouds...

Nanzong arrived; his full and flourishing bearing was no less than that of Master Zhegong. Shortly thereafter, he manifested illness and instructed his disciples, saying, "Dig a burial pit for me at Dongjian.
This is to show that even in life and death, I do not forget my devotion to my teacher. On the tenth day of the sixth month, [he passed away].
After bathing, he wrote a verse and passed away (from the lineage of Jingshan Yan).
Chan Master Pengl of Shijie at Shuanglin in Wuzhou ascended the hall and spoke, citing Chan Master Mingzhao Qian.
One day, when the weather was cold, as the assembly had just gathered, Mingzhao said, "The wind is quite stiff; let us return to a warm place to deliberate," and he immediately retired.

The Abbot arrived at the hall. As the assembly followed him there and stood in formation, he called out, "As soon as you enter this warm room, you immediately start nodding off," and with his staff, he drove them all down at once.
He then spoke this verse: "The head was already stiff and perverse; Yet you further bury yourself in warmth."
Instead, it causes those of a thousand ages to become mere traces; one has eaten Linji’s white rice in vain (Jingshan Yan’s successor).
When Qian Chan Master of Tian Tong and Bian Shan in the Qingyuan era cited the karmic conditions of Li Ao’s visit to Yaoshan, he offered this verse:
"Valuing the ear while despising the eye, He draws the golden arrow from behind his back. Looking up at the blue sky, The arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla."
The monk Guixiang spoke in verse: "I resolved my will to travel south to inquire about the True Cause, Yet not a single word of that 'True Cause' have I heard.
The corners of my tattered, frayed *kāṣāya* robe Have stirred up several fragments of cloud upon the Lingxiao Peak. The Bodhisattva Guanyin spoke in verse:
The spiral topknot curls like emerald on a spring island; green robes are scattered amidst the cold morning clouds.
Seeking the sound, one simply follows the current—what need is there to speak of the "True Contemplation" or the "Pure Contemplation"? (By Yan of Mount Jing)
Chan Master Tanchun of Kuchun at Pingjiang Huqiu ascended the hall and said: "I cite Chan Master Chang of Damei, who asked Mazu, 'What is the Buddha?
Mazu replied, 'This very mind is the Buddha. The Master said: 'Do you wish to know where Mazu’s point lies?
Water flows cold from the edge of the rock; wind comes fragrant from within the flowers. (Jingshan Yan was his successor.)
Chan Master Wen of Longxi addressed the assembly: "Without marks and without form, it is fundamentally still and vast. The moment you try to lift your eyes, it has already receded afar.
Leaning quietly upon the meditation cushion, there is nothing more to do; Outside the window, a single cry of "Pobingjiao! (Mother’s cake! rings out. (Jingshan Yan’s lineage)
Chan Master Daoyuan of Dongshan at Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang was the son of the Huang family from Lianjiang, Fujian.
He studied at Baiyun Monastery in his home prefecture and traveled throughout the two provinces of Zhejiang. Finally, he arrived at Jiangshan, where he met Chan Master Zeweng Yan.

While in the master’s room, upon being presented with the koan "The very mind is Buddha," he attained realization. He subsequently took charge of Qingliang Monastery in Fenghua and later moved to Mount Huqiu in Suzhou. Above...
The Master struck the meditation platform. Holding up his staff, he said: "Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout—these are all but worn-out, discarded implements.
Tell me, with what does Huqiu benefit people? He struck the ground with his staff and said: "Without relying on tongs or hammers, I forge Buddhas and patriarchs."
"Accustomed to breaking chopsticks to stir the vast ocean. He threw down his staff and descended from the seat.

When Xu Zhicheng, the Military Commissioner of Jian'an, raised the master from San-shan to Xuefeng, he arrived at Guangxiao Temple in Jianning, where he left behind a verse and passed away (Jingshan Yan was his successor).
Chan Master Huihong of Zhiyan at Daci Temple in Qingyuan was a native of Xinchang, Yuezhou. His secular surname was Zhu.
At the time of his birth, his mother dreamed that the High Chan Master Shifo entered her bedchamber; she awoke and he was born.

When the Master was sixteen years old, he received the tonsure and ordination under Shifo Jingyin and went to visit Zeweng Yan of Mount Jing. Zeweng asked him, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Yue."
Zhou Yan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "Jingci. Yan said, "What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? The Master hesitated.
Yan, with a stern expression, said, "You answered me clearly and in full detail when I first questioned you; now that I ask about the matter of traveling on pilgrimage, [why do you hesitate]?"
He was utterly bewildered as to what he was being obstructed by. The Master said, "You have come today to see the Abbot. Yang said, "I take pity on you as a newcomer;
go to the meditation hall. Yang later moved to Tiantong. When the Master went to attend him there again, the Master raised the koan:
"It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. The Master said, "Where the venomous dragon passes, no grass grows. Yang said, "For now, I am glad there is no connection. The Master—
He said: "Entering the water, he saw a tall man. Yan then shouted. Zhongxian Yue Wang invited him to reside at Chongbao Temple. He ascended the hall and said:

"Amidst the heaps of red dust, four autumns have passed. Having tested the various quarters, the bowl has slipped from the shoulder. Suddenly, the prow of the boat is lightly turned, and one comes back to sell Yangzhou within one's own house.

Chan Master Siming Siqui of Qingyuanshouguo Temple was the son of the Yu family of Shanyin. On the occasion of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa, he ascended the hall and said:
"The true Dharma-body of the Buddha is like empty space. Why, then, on the fifteenth day of the second month, did he go beneath the twin śāla trees and put on such a display of death?
After a long silence, he said: "The shadows of bamboo sweep the steps, yet the dust does not stir; the lunar disc pierces the sea..."
No trace upon the water. [The Master] ascends the hall. Guizong cuts the snake; Bimao holds up the pitchfork; Heshan beats the drum; Zhaozhou drinks tea.
Opening a shop at the crossroads of the street, buying and selling with ready cash—no credit allowed. (Jingshan Yan and ten others follow.)
Chan Master Fazhou of Biyu at Daochang in Huzhou once offered this praise for the Fish Basket Guanyin:
"The crescent moon is stamped alone upon the gate of the sea; Chasing waves and following currents, he is no true man.
Where his two hands reach out to lift them up for others, He instead exchanges fish eyes for bright pearls. (Yuwang Yin’s successor)
Chan Master Wujie Guan received the Dharma from Chan Master Yin of Yuwang. He inscribed the following on a portrait of the World-Honored One leaving the palace:

Chan Master Wujing Che of Tianting Monastery during the Qingyuan era ascended the hall and, citing the case of Master Yantou, when a monk asked:
"In the midst of vast dust and confusion, how does one act as the host? Yantou replied: "A copper *sarāva* filled to the brim with oil. He then offered this verse: "A hundred thousand..."

Chan Master Niaofeng Ding composed a verse in praise of Master Xuansha, saying: "A green raincoat, unwilling to trade for a golden seal;

(The two masters above are successors of the Tian Tong lineage.)

Taking his seat in the abbot’s quarters, the mountain monk says today: "I shall open the gates of hell and invite all people throughout the great earth to construct that very hell."
Karma. One will experience the retribution of hell. If there is a single person who attains Buddhahood and becomes a Patriarch, I vow not to attain Perfect Enlightenment...

[Ascending the hall: Heaven is high and earth is deep; the sun waxes and the moon wanes. To fully uphold [the Dharma] or to only partially uphold it is as vast a distance as that between heaven and earth.
Chan Master Can spent his entire life only knowing how to put on his robes and eat his meals. When he heard others speak the two words "Buddha-dharma," it was like the wind passing over a tree.

He released the White Elephant King; he could not be found anywhere across the earth. [The Master] picks up his staff: "There is only this one thing, which belongs neither to the old nor the new.

Chan Master Wumen Huikai of Huanglong during the Longxing era was a native of Liangzhu in Hangzhou. His clan name was Liang.

The myriad phenomena and the entire cosmos bow their heads together; Mount Sumeru leaps and dances the Three Platforms. The next day, he entered the room wishing to communicate what he had realized. Guàn (Zhaozhou) immediately said:

In the sixth year of the Chunyou era, by imperial decree, he was appointed to open the mountain at Huguo Renhuang Temple. He ascended the hall and said:
"If a person recognizes the mind, there is not an inch of earth in the great earth. When the ancients spoke thus, Huanglong would not have agreed. If...

The Elder Cishou only knew how to set sail with the current; he was unable to steer against the wind. Huanglong, however, was not like this:

having cast aside both right and wrong, he invites you to realize it within right and wrong. Why is this so? "How many times the black winds have tossed the great waves, yet never once did we hear of the fishing boat capsizing.

a single flake of snow upon a red-hot furnace. (Ganyuan Ying)

This immediately deviates [from the truth]. (Yuan’an Meng comments: “The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor resent that they have one body too many.

Mixing water with mud—how busy with such trivial matters! He has pierced through it all, yet how utterly perverse! Though he may indeed grasp the Emperor’s intent, what can he do?
His entire body is plunged into the cauldron of boiling oil. (Yue of Lingyin, the successor).
Chan Master Zhongqian Daxie of Xuedou in Qingyuan was the son of the Ying family of Yingwu.

In his youth, upon seeing the *Mind-King Inscription* by the Great Master Fu, he resolved to leave the household life. He first visited Xian’an, who, recognizing his potential yet wishing to test him, suppressed him, saying:
"You have not eliminated the habitual tendencies of a Confucian scholar; how can you study the Way? To reach the state of great rest and great cessation, you must be like a wooden puppet."

He departed. Inspired by his teacher’s exhortation, he redoubled his efforts, practicing day and night without ceasing. One day, he suddenly attained realization and named his state "Great Rest" (Dàxiē).
Later, he went to study under Songyuan Yue. One day, in the meditation hall, Songyuan brought up the story of Bimozhe holding up his staff.
The Master attained a great awakening. He ascended the hall and, citing Master Ying’an Hua’s question to Master Mi’an Jie, “What is the True Dharma Eye?
Jie replied, “A broken sand-pot. Hua nodded in approval. He then offered this verse:
“A marble pellet carved from white jade, A bronze giant cast from pure gold. This ancient wares, unsold for a thousand years, Cannot help but trouble us even now.”

Chan Master Nuohan Zhao (Lingyin Yue’s successor) composed a verse titled “Reminiscing of Huating”: “My entire livelihood is but a single fishing boat; When the jeweled fish falls into my hands, I pull it in.
I have come here, yet do not behold the Master’s personal instruction; The willows by the bank lean gently, dipping into the azure stream. (Lingyin)
Chan Master Yun’an Puyan of Daochang Monastery in Huzhou (a successor of the former master) inscribed this eulogy for the portrait of Zhaozhou:
"Pointlessly he held up the seven-pound robe; How many practitioners have applied their minds to investigate it! They all take refuge in Qingzhou, Unaware of the spring."

In the region south of the Yangtze River (Lingyin, successor of Yue), there was Chan Master Jili Tan of Suzhou’s Tiger Hill. He first resided at Yanqing in Siming and later moved to Qionglong in Suzhou.
Later, he arrived at Huqiu. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
Lin replied, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains. The Master said, "How has the rabbit ever left its burrow?
If someone were to ask Yanqing, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe? I would simply answer him: 'The fish bought on the boat is especially delicious; treading through the snow...'"
The wine bought from the market is doubly fragrant. [Ascending the hall: "In every thought, Śākyamuni appears in the world; at every moment, Maitreya descends to be born.
Instantly transcending the time before heaven and earth were divided, one does not traverse the rungs of a ladder but overturns the precious abode—proceeding directly in this very way."
"One can open immeasurable Dharma gates; one can expound hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings. [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, struck once, and said:
"Immeasurable Dharma gates and hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings are all completely shattered and pulverized right here.
Do you know where Tiger Hill lands? [He] leans on the staff: 'The patriarchs could not settle it; the calamity reaches their descendants. (Yue of Lingyin, successor).
Chan Master Shaoshi Guangmu of Ruiyan in Taizhou ascended the hall. He cited Chan Master Xiang of Caoshan:
once, while a monk was standing in attendance, Caoshan said, "The Way-farer is quite hot. The monk replied, "Yes. Caoshan asked, "As for this heat, where do you go to avoid it?
The monk replied, "I avoid it within the cauldrons and the furnace embers. Caoshan asked, "And as for those cauldrons and furnace embers..."
[The monk] said, "How else can one evade it? [Dongshan] replied, "The various sufferings cannot reach him. The Master composed a verse: "The three eyes on the crown of the head are blinded;
One wanders freely amidst boiling cauldrons and burning coals. If you say the various sufferings cannot reach him, Exactly where could they ever find a place to land? (Successor of Lingyin Yue)
Chan Master Shankaikai of Jinshan on Mount Zhenjiang ascended the hall and, citing the story of Mian’s “Broken Sand Pot,” offered this verse:
Fayan brought it up and was already deceiving himself; Needlessly, he wrongly matched it to the broken sand pot. Now it pervades the entire world, impossible to conceal;
It brings calamity upon the monastic groves and their descendants. (Yue of Lingyin, his successor)
Chan Master Wuxiang Fan of Xuedou in Mingzhou ascended the hall and said: "Master Zhaozhou once remarked, 'As soon as there is right and wrong, one becomes distracted and loses one's mind.
Is there still any possibility of answering? A monk cited this to Lopu, who tapped his teeth."

The monk also recounted this to Yunju. Yunju said, "Why bother? When the monk returned and recounted it to Zhaozhou, Zhaozhou said, "In the South, there are many who lose their bodies and forfeit their lives. The monk said, "Please, Master, provide an example. Just as Zhaozhou was about to repeat the previous story, the monk pointed to a monk standing nearby and said, "This monk, having finished his meal, speaks such words! One standing on the bottom sees those at the top; one standing on the top sees those sitting at the bottom. Alas, old Zhaozhou! Seeing ghosts with one’s own eyes in broad daylight (Yongyue, successor of Lingyin).
Layman Lu You, Secretariat Supervisor, courtesy name Wuguang, style name Fangong, was a native of Shanyin. He frequently visited Songyuan Yue.

At Lingyin Monastery, the Master (Heshang) asked with composure, "May I hear about the study of mind-to-mind transmission? Fayan Wenyue replied, "Since it is a transmission of the mind, how could it be obtained through hearing?
Layman Xianzhu nodded his head in silent understanding and then presented this verse: "How many times have I driven my carriage into the imperial capital?
Whenever I encountered a monk, my eyes were equally clear and bright. Today, for the first time, I see the distinctiveness of our school: It speaks neither of existence nor of non-existence."
Regarding the essential point of "listening with the eyes" (there were fourteen people in total, including Lingyin Yue’s successors):
Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Jingshan in Lin’an was the son of Xun of the Changjiang lineage in Wuxin; his mother was Guo.

From birth, he was broad-shouldered and short-statured, and his natural disposition far surpassed that of ordinary men. As he grew older, he attempted the imperial examination for the jinshi degree but did not succeed. Thereupon, he...

He left the household life and traveled to various lecture halls to study the sutras and śāstras. In the *Renzi* year of the Shaoxī era, he emerged from the Gorges and wandered through the regions of Jing and Chu.
At that time, Caoyuan Sheng was appearing in the world at Miaoguo; the Master went there to visit him. Upon hearing the words spoken as he entered the gate, he attained a realization.

He was assigned to attend to the incense in the meditation hall, where the old master [Caoyuan] did not spare him his heavy fists and painful blows day and night. Consequently, much of the Master’s lifelong views and knowledge vanished without a trace.
Xiang followed the Master to Mount Gui, where he attended him for another three years. Then, departing to travel through Zhejiang, he offered this verse of farewell:

"There remains but one pair of hands in my state of poverty; I shall scratch the itchy places of all quarters toward the west. Initially, he took up residence at Guangxiao Temple in Jiahe, where his reputation reached the imperial court.
The Prince of Wei, Zhongxian, issued an official decree appointing him to Jiangshan. All the estates of Jiangshan were situated along the river.
The region was prone to flooding; the low-lying fields frequently yielded no harvest. The Master endured hunger while proclaiming the Way, begging for alms to support his disciples.

For thirteen years he lived there without ever showing a trace of weariness. In the Jiaxi year, Jihai (1259), Minister Cao Bin of Dongquan, who was the Governor of Min, heard of the Master’s reputation and sent an invitation from Drum Mountain (Gushan).
However, before he could depart, a summons arrived from Xuefeng. He took up his duties there for half a year, after which [the call] came from Tiantong.

The imperial decree was issued, and the assembly gathered like the sea. King Ashoka vacated his seat, and [the Master] assumed the duties of abbot. Moving between the two mountains, he ascended the hall and said:
"The tools used by Tiantong are not employed here at Yuwang; the tools used here at Yuwang are not employed at Tiantong.
Although they are thus not employed, where they are not employed, their utility is more than sufficient. A single arrow brings down two eagles, following the hand."

Ascending the hall at the end of the summer retreat: In the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment, every dust mote has its own path; going and coming are cut off, and past and present are suddenly emptied.
"Thirteen there, fifteen here"—the sequence does not differ by even a hair’s breadth. How laughable that the Yellow-faced Gautama still does not know where he has landed!
[When] Xian was at Mount Jing, one day he suddenly ascended the seat to take his leave of the assembly.
When the World-Honored One was about to enter *nirvāṇa*, he addressed the assembly, saying: "You should carefully contemplate my body, the color of purple-polished gold.
Gaze upon it until you have had your fill; do not let yourselves regret it later. What exists today may well be gone tomorrow. The Master said:
"For forty-nine years, the World-Honored One exhausted every skill and artifice. Yet when the time of his departure arrived, he could not find life when he sought it."
He could not be stopped from dying. Today, this mountain monk acts when he wishes to act and goes when he wishes to go; even the eight-armed Nala cannot restrain him.
At the end of the night, he rose from his seat and passed away after a brief interval. He was eighty-two years of age. Upon cremation, there were countless relics of five colors.
In accordance with his final instructions, his remains were brought back to be interred at Yushan Hermitage in Jinling. His disciples divided half of them among themselves.
At Chāngpú Tián (Jiànfú Sēngsì), Lín'ān Jìngcí Qīngxī Yuán Chánshī ascended the hall and said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he occupied a single sitting mat.
Yet, when Shen Guang paid him three prostrations, it was all at once taken over by him. This has caused the descendants of later generations to each divide [the territory] for themselves."
Defining the boundaries. Zen monks pluck the weeds and gaze at the wind; morning in Wu, evening in Yue; south to Tiantai, north to Wutai.
Upon the tip of the staff, beneath the soles of the straw sandals—have you ever trodden there yet? After a long silence, he said: "Above all, do not tread there" (Tiantong Jue’s successor).
Chan Master Xixi Xi of Gongan in Jingzhou ascended the hall and said: "The place where mind-mind is shallow is, in truth, most profound;
The path of the Way is remote and deep, with no one reaching it. If you walk too fast, you will not tread upon it; If you walk too slow, you will miss the point.
How many times did Shaolin sit through the blossoming of spring flowers? Yet I still recall the Western-come Hu Daomo. (Tiantong Jue’s Verse)
Chan Master Yuet-tan Yuan of Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou ascends the hall to open the furnace for the winter retreat: "Everyone guards the sky within the jar;
When earth is overturned and heaven is turned upside down, I am not like them. With one direct stroke, sparks fly forth; The Luojiang River has burned the boat of Master Xie.
In praise of Pig-Headed Monk (Zhoutou Heshang), he said: "Bloody and raw—this is the heart-mind of the ancient Buddha. How many times has it been raised up? Who is there to..."
Zhiyin (Successor of Tiantong Jing).
Chan Master Jichuang Youzhao of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan was the son of the Deng family of Min County.
At that time, Kuchan Jing was propagating the Way at Yishan. The Master went to visit him. One day, Jing asked: "Since first seeing the peach blossoms..."
Later, until the present day, he has not doubted further. "Wherein lies his state of non-doubt? The Master laughed heartily and walked out. Jingshen approved of this.
When Jingshen moved to Lingyin, the Master served as the Head of the Inner Records (*neiji*). To visit his aged mother, he returned home;
there, Zhao Gong Ruyou, the Military Governor of Min, invited him to open the Dharma at Dongshan Dacheng. He subsequently moved to Huangbo in Fuzhou, where he was appointed by imperial decree.

Jiangxin. Later, he moved to Yujı. Encountering a natural disaster, he exerted all his strength to rebuild it. He memorialized the imperial court, which granted him gold and silk to construct a precious *śarīra* stūpa.
He ascended the hall and said: "The six sense objects are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment. The crows caw, 'ya ya.'"
The magpie caws, the magpie caws; north of the river, south of the river. The tide rises, the tide falls; in the third month of spring, flowers and grasses are fragrant.
Where does Sudhana seek the pavilions? (A shout from Tiantong Jingci).
Chan Master Yugu Yuanzhi of Fashi Temple in Quanzhou was the son of the Xue family of Changxi. After attaining realization while studying under Tiantong, he presented this verse on mountain dwelling:
"A saffron robe, patched a thousand times over, Leaning against a pine, I stroke my belly and watch the clouds fly.
When someone asks about the joy of dwelling in the mountains, I tell them: deep in spring, the bamboo shoots and ferns are lush. The first month of the Bingyin year of the Xianchun era.
He sat cross-legged, wrote a verse, and passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the South Monastery of Mount Gu (Tiantong Jing was his successor).
Master Taigu Xian of Baoen ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it does not involve the workings of thought or intention;
it has nothing to do with silent illumination or the forgetting of the self. To attain a state of transparent clarity, you must undergo a 'breakthrough' of sweat. Now tell me, what is this sweat?"
After descending from the seat, he suddenly called to his attendant, "Bring me the fan! [He held it up] and ascended the hall.
"Monks of the Zen school who travel and wander about, brushing aside the weeds and gazing at the wind, must first recognize the path;

only then will you succeed. If the path is not mistaken, then east, west, south, and north—everywhere becomes your home. Should you stray even slightly, there will be single-signposts every five li and double-milestones every ten li. Where would you go?"
"Furthermore, it is right there. [Tiantong says: "He throws down his staff and says: 'Look beneath your feet.
(Tiantong Jing’s Succession) Master Chun of Jie had studied under Master Jing for a long time and attained realization. On the Buddha’s Birthday, he wrote this verse:
"The poisonous seeds of Vairambha wind open into poisonous flowers; They add another cup to Yunmen’s drunkenness. Today, the colors at He Feng Bridge are ominous; A pale mist..."
Sparse rain washes the yellow plum blossoms. (The *Zadu hai* records that this verse was composed by Xiyuan; its source remains unknown. [The above seven masters include Tiantong Jingsi].)
Master Shuangshan Yuan of Tiger Hill in Pingjiang cited the story of Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, who dreamed of a divine being who exhorted him to arouse the bodhicitta.
The following day, the Emperor asked his court ministers, "How does one arouse the bodhicitta? None of the ministers could respond. Xuedou, acting on their behalf, said:
"Truly something rarely heard in antiquity or today. Biefeng Yin, acting on their behalf, said: "The words of the King are like a fine thread; their issue is like a thick cord."
The Master’s Verse says: Ten thousand miles of songs celebrate the Sage’s transformation; In gentle breezes and light rains, woodcutters and farmers rejoice.
Were it not for the three cries at Mount Song, Who would know this true Great Peace beyond all forms? The Verse on the Wall Paintings in the Two Corridors of Cold Spring:
Within every single atom is the firm and dense body; changing heads and faces, it shifts its spirit. Who knows that striking the west wall is actually the east wall?
All are people from the assembly at Vulture Peak. (Yinjing Rou’s Successor)
Chan Master Xuanzou Xingduan of Jingshan in Lin’an was the son of the He family of Línghǎi. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations; his mother was surnamed Chén.
From birth he was exceptionally gifted, and as a youth he abstained from meat. At twelve he left home to become a monk, and at eighteen he received full ordination.
Regarding all literary texts, he did not rely on instruction from a teacher. Initially, he visited Zangzou Zhen at Jingshan, who asked him, "Where are you from? The Master—
Yangshan said, "It is Taizhou. Yantou Zhen gave a shout. The Master spread his sitting cloth; Zhen shouted again. The Master withdrew his sitting cloth.
Zhen said, "I grant you thirty blows. Go to the hall for practice. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
One day, while standing in attendance, Zhen said, "There are no monks in Southern Quanzhou. The Master asked, "What about the Master? Zhen struck him. The Master caught the staff and said:
"Do not say that it is better to have no monks. Zhen nodded his head in agreement. He then ordered [the Master] to enter the service of the administration.

When Zhen passed away, the Master went to Jingci Monastery, where he once referred to himself as a native of the "Cold and Pickers" (Hanshi) village. Later, he was invited to reside at Mount Jingshan as the First Seat.

In the *Gengzi* year of the Dade era, by special imperial decree, he was granted the title Chan Master Huiwen Zhengbian. In the *Renzi* year of the Huangqing era, he moved to Lingyin Monastery, where an imperial edict was issued to establish [a formal assembly].

At the Great Assembly on Land and Water at Mount Jin, he was commanded to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma. Upon the conclusion of the ceremony, he entered the imperial presence for an audience and was granted the honorary title "Buddha-Sun Shining Universally.
Taking his leave of the Emperor, he returned south to retire in seclusion at West Hill in Liangzhu. (The year) was Zhizhi Renxu.
The seat at Mount Jing was vacant, and the Master was invited to fill it. Having been bestowed the golden robe three times, for twenty years his feet had not crossed the threshold of his quarters;
yet those who admired his Way gathered like scales of fish until there was no room to contain them. Once, the Master examined a newly arrived monk, saying, "From what direction do you come, O Sage?
Where do you dwell, O Spirit? The monk replied, "I am right here before Your Majesty. The Master said, "You are a self-fabricating Chan practitioner."
"Like hemp, like millet. Go to the hall. [He] further examined a monk, saying: "The chessboard stone will break open your skull; the bowl-basin pool will soak and rot your soles.
As the monk was about to answer, the Master gave a shout. [He] again examined a monk, saying: "Tearing apart Mount Hua, its beauty reaches the heavens;
releasing the Yellow River, it flows clear to the bottom. Setting that aside for a moment, what is the fundamental reality?"
"Bring me a phrase from the path of the earth. As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master struck him. The Master used scolding, rage, and abuse as compassionate and guiding instruction;
he acted contrary to worldly sentiment to practice the Way of Great Publicity. All of the Master’s benefit for others was performed in secret; he spoke not of it until the day he died.
On the fourth day of the eighth month of the Xinsi year of the Zhizheng era, he manifested slight illness and asked:
The attendant said, "Calling it has already ceased; inhaling it has not yet been relinquished. I send word to all sources of suffering:
as for those who come and those who do not come—what is 'those who come and those who do not come'? The attendant remained silent. After a long while, the Master said, "Look in five days.
When the time arrived, he bathed, changed his robes, and wrote a verse to bid farewell to the assembly, saying: "Originally there is no arising or ceasing; how could there be going or coming?"

He arrived. The ice-river burst into flame; the iron trees blossomed. He cast down his writing brush, extended one foot, and passed away. His remains stayed in the shrine for seven days, the complexion remaining as if alive.
His entire body was interred in the Jizhao Pagoda Courtyard (at Mount Jing, by Zhen Si).

Chan Master Liaowan of Jiaoxin Mountain in Wenzhou was born into the Jin clan of Linchuan. He was thin and physically frail in appearance. At the age of fifteen, he gained renown for his literary studies.
On the day he received the tonsure, a *zhī* fungus grew from the pivot of his door. Later, while traveling to study under various masters, he encountered Dongsou, who was leading Nanping;

Dongsou appointed the Master as his scribe (*jǐ*). Once, while passing by a shrine to a deity, he saw paper ashes swirling upward, and he suddenly attained a state of liberation, forgetting all that he had previously realized.

He immediately informed the Elder. The Elder interrogated him, and he was subsequently granted formal approval (*anujñā*). He traveled to Tiantai, where the assembly requested that he open a Dharma hall at Hanyan.

Offering incense, he became a successor to Dongsou. After more than three years, he moved to Zituo in Xianju; ten years later, he moved to Shushan; and another ten years later, he resided at Jiangxin.
Whenever his mind was slightly dissatisfied, he would immediately abandon his post. Although there were several hundred monks in the temple, they entreated him to remain with tears in their eyes.
No one could detain him. It happened that Master Yuejian of Mount Lu sent a boat to welcome the Master back to Dongxi.
When Master Yuejian passed away, the community at Kaixian again requested his presence, but the Master firmly declined. One day, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying:
"This staff—used by the Seven Patriarchs of the Western Heaven and the Two or Three Patriarchs of this land—none of the old monks throughout the world have been able to handle it."
Today it has fallen into the hands of Kaixian; without beginning and without end, he can release and can gather in, transcending both form and name, able to grant and able to seize.
Although it is thus, it is only for those of middling or inferior capacity. What if a person of the highest caliber were to suddenly arrive?
[With his staff, he draws a circle] and lets this one move pass. (Huangqing Year 1, Gou).
He sat upright in meditation despite his critical illness and declined medical treatment. After seven days had passed, he instructed that preparations be made for a bath and a change of robes.

He did not even base his conclusion on the evidence. Taking up his staff, he asked: "What is the Buddha? Treading barefoot upon lotus flowers.
"What is the matter beyond the Buddha? Carved beams and painted rafters. He then threw down the staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Ascending the hall for a discourse, he said:
"The five thousand and forty-eight volumes can all be expressed in a single phrase. He then rose and said: "Stand here and wait!"
The assembly gathered and he descended from his seat. His verse at the time of death said: "Eighty-three years—what kind of thing is this?
The cypress tree attains Buddhahood; empty space falls to the ground. After his cremation, the *śarīra* relics were brilliantly clear; his teeth and his prayer beads remained unbroken.
(He was the successor of Jingci Ying).
Zen Master Yunwu Zixian of Shuanglin in Wuzhou was the son of the Ye family of Kuocang and the ninth-generation descendant of Zen Master Wugui Xing.
Initially, he studied under Jingshou Jue at Lingyin, and subsequently visited Dongshou Ying at Jingci.
Cizhang served as the Secretary of the Monastery. One day, while composing a commentary on the Buddha’s Enlightenment, he said, “I have brought forth the essence of vision at midnight.

The Old Man (the Master) replied, “Why do you not say that you have extinguished the essence of vision at midnight? At these words, the Master’s thighs trembled involuntarily and sweat poured from him, as if a thick veil had been lifted from his eyes.

He then clearly perceived the place where the Old Man extended his hand to save others. Later, he appeared in the world at Shuanglin, was subsequently transferred to Zhiye, and [reigned] during the Renqing era.

On the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month, while conversing and laughing with his guests, he suddenly commanded an attendant monk to fetch a brush and wrote a verse, after which he passed away (Jingci Ying succeeded him;

Chan Master Huiji Yuanxi of Fozhi Temple at Mount Jing in Lin’an was the son of the Tang family of Yuzhang.
He and his elder brother, Yuanling, both studied for the jinshi examinations. Once Yuanling had passed the exams, the Master followed Minggong of the Western Mountains to receive the tonsure.
He was about to travel abroad. His mother provided him with silver as travel funds, but the Master remarked that wealth would surely lead to the loss of one's resolve; he thus politely declined them.
Hearing that Wugu initially propagated the teachings at Yujiji, he went there to rely upon him. Gu was astonished by his conversation and kept him in his service.
During the Zhizhi era of the Yuan dynasty, the Imperial Preceptor Yang Lianzhenru, acting on imperial decree to retrieve the śarīra relics of Yuyang, personally visited [the Master].
The Master requested a record of the origins and conclusion of the śarīra relics, and consequently invited [the author] to accompany him. The Master said, "I have an elderly mother;

her survival or demise after the war cannot be known. He then took leave to return to Jiangxi. Yuanling had previously served as the Vice Prefect of Linjiang and died in the cause while following Wen Tianxiang in raising troops;
his mother alone remained at home. The Master supported her with such filial piety that he became renowned for it. (Yuanzhen 2)
In his later years, he became the abbot of Baizhang. He resided there for twelve years until the beginning of the Dade era, when he accepted the invitation from Jingci Monastery.
On the day he entered the monastery, officials from the Zhongshusheng and the Xuanzhengyuan came to welcome him, and he was invited to propagate the fundamental tenets of the school.
Eminent monks from all quarters gathered like spokes in a wheel. Ascending the hall, he said: "I sit alone upon the Great Hero Peak; Cold ashes cannot be stirred to glow red. A single star..."

Suddenly, if there is one who breaks through the azure sky and knocks over Mount Sumeru..."
"Bottom. He said, "Do not say that the knotting is not firm and dense. After a long silence, he said, "A net covering the heavens, hundreds and thousands of layers.
He resided there for seven years and then moved to Mount Jing. Shortly thereafter, he took up his staff and returned to the foot of Mount Nanping.

When the disciples of Baizhang and Dayang heard that the Master had retired from public life, they vied with one another to come and invite him. Unable to refuse them, the Master finally returned to Mount Yang. He resided there for three years.

As he was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, he wrote by hand a letter of farewell to those with whom he had associated. He further composed a verse of parting for the assembly, cast aside his brush, and passed away.
His worldly age was eighty-two. His entire body was enshrined and buried beneath the Jīnī Stone.
His disciples who were in Hangzhou divided his fingernails and hair to erect stupas at Jingci, Xiyin, and Yuyang Guansi.
Chan Master Yunfeng Miaogao of Jingshan in Qingyuan was a native of Changxi in Fuzhou. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.

His mother, surnamed Ruan, dreamed of an infant on a pond sitting cross-legged upon a lotus flower with palms joined; she reached down and took him up in her hands. Upon waking, she gave birth to the Master, who was thus named Mengchi (Dream-Pond).

His spirit and countenance were exceptionally refined and penetrating; he was fond of books and applied himself diligently to study, especially the Buddhist scriptures, and earnestly requested to study the path of transcendence.

He left home to receive the full precepts. When Emperor Yingzong saw Chan Master Wencan of Yangxi, their spiritual resonance was in perfect accord, and he appointed him to keep the keys to the treasury.
One day, when Wencan raised the analogy, "It is like a bull passing through a window frame: its head, horns, and four hooves have all passed through; why then can its tail not pass?
the Master attained a sudden and great realization. He then said: "The whale swallows the ocean until it is exhausted, revealing..."
Shanzhu (珊珠) heard of this and granted his permission. When the seat at Mount Jiangshan was vacant, he accepted the imperial decree to reside there for thirteen years.
His followers numbered more than five thousand. In the year of Yihai during the Deyou era, the temple was attacked by troops.

A soldier pointed a blade at the Master, who extended his neck and said, "If you wish to kill me, then kill me; my head is not a whetstone for your blade. His words and expression were entirely devoid of fear. The soldiers—
The layman was moved by this transformation; he cast away his sword and departed. In the seventeenth year of the Zhizhi era (1280), he moved to Mount Jing.
When the temple suffered a fire, the Master’s arrival caused it to immediately return to its former splendor. He addressed the assembly: "The preceding thought is ordinary;
the succeeding thought is sacred. Cut them in two with one stroke—do not hesitate any longer. Thus, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the butcher Guang'e cast down his butcher’s blade.

He then declared, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas. Although this was so, if one lacks the strength to lift a cauldron or pull up a mountain, it is not easy to ride a black steed from a thousand *li* away.
At that time, there were those in the capital who slandered the Chan school. The Master said, "This is a matter of great importance for the Dharma;
I shall contend for it even at the cost of my life. He subsequently went to the imperial court and, by imperial decree, convened the followers of the various schools to debate before the throne.
Emperor Shizu of the Yuan dynasty asked, "What is the fundamental principle of Chan? The Master replied, "Pure wisdom is wondrously perfect; its essence is fundamentally empty and still.
It cannot be reached by seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing, nor by thought, deliberation, or discrimination.

The Emperor questioned him repeatedly, and the Master enumerated the patriarchs of India and China, including the causes and conditions regarding the staff and shouts of Deshan and Linji, totaling over two thousand words. The Emperor then issued another decree.
He advanced before the Emperor’s dais and engaged in a series of debates with the slanderer. The slanderer was left speechless and defeated. Emperor Shizu was greatly pleased.
The Master took his leave of the throne and returned south. Addressing the assembly, he said: "I originally intended to remain hidden deep within mountain caves, passing my time in seclusion.

I did not expect that the sun would shine upon me and the heavens would look down, making it difficult to escape the reach of the Great Transformation. He further said: "With the patched robe covering my head, all matters come to rest; at this moment, I am a mountain monk."
Neither was this the case. When Jing Mountain suffered a disaster and was destroyed by fire, the Master said to the assembly, "It is simply that I owe a debt to this mountain from my past lives.
He then exerted all his strength to rebuild it, turning the slope of the Hall into a pond, and other buildings were completed in succession.
On the seventeenth day of the sixth month in the thirtieth year of the Zhizhi era (1343), he wrote a verse and passed away. Later, a stupa was built at the western foot of the temple (Jingci Wensi).
Master Tiesheng Zhiming of He Mountain in Huzhou was the son of the Wang family of Changxi, Fudang.
Having met Master Wenyue of Yanxi at Jingci Monastery, he visited him morning and evening for a long time before finally receiving certification of his realization.

He requested paper and wrote in large characters: "The net is cast aside; there is no more evasion. The waves of the great ocean are stilled; empty space is revealed alone.

Chan Master Zhihong Jian of Tian Tong in Qingyuan, during his initial tenure at Zhenru in Qingyuan and later his move to Tian Tong, ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddhas are not real; they preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings. The Bodhisattvas possess wisdom, yet their vision of nature is not clear."
White clouds have no intentionality, yet they shed rain upon the world. The great earth has no sentimentality, yet it can cause all grasses and trees to grow.
When the ancient worthies proclaimed in this manner, they opened the way for humans and devas within the Dharma of the Four Truths; their skillful means were truly unsurpassed.
Yet, from the perspective of a patch-robed monk, how could it be anything less than ten thousand miles of white clouds? [Ascending the hall, he held up his staff. "One [has] many..."

Later, as he was about to pass away, he bathed, changed his robes, and wrote this verse: "Eighty-two years; I have been deceived by the world."

The circumstances were as follows: He performed somersaults with such vigor that he left his tracks in the Western Region; then, casting aside his pen, he sat upright and passed away (Jianfu Can was his successor).

Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. He went to visit Yunfeng Xìn, who asked, "Where do you dwell, Senior Monk?

Several plows and harrows (Huazang Jing’s lineage).

Subsequently, he presided over Jingci Monastery. He once composed the *Fuzong Xianzheng Lun* (Treatise on Supporting the School and Manifesting Orthodoxy), which Emperor Renzong examined and praised;

the Emperor bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya* and conferred the honorary title Chan Master Huiguang Puzhao Wencming Tongbian (Jingshan Ju was his successor; the two aforementioned individuals).
Master Wujie of Baolin Monastery in Wuzhou ascended the hall. "Reeds flowered against the red dock; leaves fall and the mountains reveal their bones.
It resembles Yangzhou; it vaguely recalls the state of Yue. He took up his staff, struck once, and said:
"For you, I strike through the cave of the spirit, leaving the Unranked True Person bare-boned. (Lingyin Quan’s successor).
Chan Master Wujian of Huizang at Wenzhou cited the verse on Xinghua striking Kebin, saying: Xinghua struck Kebin;
The words were intimate, yet the speech was not. From the tip of the staff, like falling raindrops, He beat forth the Jade Qilin (Huanglong Kai succeeded him).
Chan Master Wuchuan Zuyun of Lin’an ascended the hall and said: "Buddha after Buddha has expounded extensively, yet even great wisdom cannot know it.

Patriarch after Patriarch has transmitted it from one to another, yet how could ordinary sentiments fathom it? Before heaven and after earth, creation and destruction endure forever; entering death and being born again, coming and going remain unchanged.
If you can realize this, you have already entered the realm of fragmentation. If this is not yet so, I, this mountain monk, shall speak further."
To provide a footnote for this, he struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "Though one may cry until the blood flows, it is of no use;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring" (Huanglong Kuisi).
Chan Master Zong of Chou-an at Huguo Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said:
He cited Fenggan as saying to Hanshan and Shide, "If you and I go to travel to Mount Wutai, you will be of my same kind. Hanshan asked, "Why would you go to travel to Mount Wutai?
Fenggan replied, "To pay homage to Mañjuśrī. Hanshan said, "You are not of my same kind. The Master said, "Fenggan..."
The mouth opens, yet it does not reside on the tongue. Hanshan and his fellow in the same pit are no different in their soil.
When examined closely, two hunchbacks collide with one another; there likely is no upright person in this world (Huanglong Kuisi).
The lay practitioner Fangu Yu visited Chan Master Wumen Kai. Whenever he asked a question, Kai would block him head-on and say, "Not so, not so.

One day, he asked his fellow student Chou'an Zong, "What kind of insight does my teacher have that he dares to distort right from wrong before the assembly of devas and humans? Zong replied, "While I was under Wumen's guidance, I had no dharma."
"It can be attained, yet there is no Way to transmit. One only obtains two characters. The scholar asked, "What are these two characters? Zong said, "Not this, not that.

At these words, the scholar suddenly attained awakening to the state of being without a gate for others. Laywoman Shen Dao of Anji Prefecture asked, "How many phrases are there regarding the barrier of right and wrong?
The Master said, "There are four phrases. The Laywoman asked, "How do you cite these four phrases? The Master—
He said: "The first phrase—'it is,' or 'it is not'—is unacceptable. The second phrase—'it is neither'—is also unacceptable.
The third phrase—'it both is and is not'—is unacceptable. The fourth phrase—'it neither is nor is not'—is also unacceptable.
Only by transcending these four phrases can one finally behold the natural radiance of the original ground. The monk asked: "Have I transcended them? The Master said: "Yes."
"You cannot avoid it," [the Master] said. [The monk] replied, "Every person has their lot; why should I not avoid it? The Master said, "When a hen is married off, she flies after the cock;
when a dog is married off, it runs after the dog. [The monk] asked, "What is the natural splendor of the original ground?

The Master said, "The crescent moon shines upon the nine provinces; how many rejoice, and how many grieve? [The monk] said, "I do not ask about this natural splendor of the original ground. The Master—
The Master said, "Ask about that original local scenery. The scholar said, "It is that which has no marks of male or female.

The Master said, "Since there are no marks of male or female, what question could there be regarding the barrier of right and wrong? The scholar said, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is.
The scholar asked, "What is this matter that is further beyond? The Master said, "A locust bites the leg of a heron; when you ascend to heaven, I shall ascend with you."
(Huanglong Kaishi and the four aforementioned masters).
Chan Master Zhengning Wanshan of Gushan in Fuzhou was a native of Taicheng in Longshu. He entered Min to pay respects to Master Guofeng Xiu.
When Xiu posed the koan regarding the dog having no Buddha-nature, the Master could not answer. After more than half a year had passed, he finally attained realization.
At the innermost depths, he then uttered this verse: "Zhaozhou says there is no [Buddha-nature]; the arrow does not miss its mark. Striking it, hitting it—completely saving, completely killing.
Xiu said, "You have attained it, yet you have not yet reached the ultimate. One day, Xiu raised the story of Deshan seeing Longtan and asked, "Where is the place where Deshan reached his own ground?

The Master covered Xiu’s mouth with his hand and immediately spoke this verse: The iron ox has no horns; The wooden horse has no tail. If you wish to see the true person, Look at the face before your parents were born.
The pool was no longer visible; the dragon did not appear. His entire body had already entered the Hall of the Empty King. Returning from his dream, he suddenly heard the dawn oriole singing.
The spring breeze had blown away all the peach petals. Xiu said, "Only today do you realize that the Great Sage of Sizhou does not manifest in Yangzhou.
"Protect yourself well," [the Master] said, and subsequently appointed him to attend to the incense. After a long time, the Grand Tutor, Chancellor Jia Wei...

The Duke (Guogong) issued an edict requesting him to reside at Gushan. Upon entering the monastery, he ascended the hall. It has been only three days since his arrival; I have been busy attending to social obligations.
The lantern and the pillar have been consulting one another in great detail. But tell me, what were they discussing? He struck the meditation seat.

"Last night the blue sky was calm and the winds and waves stilled; a single bright moon reflected upon the Luojiang River. [He] ascended the hall on the first day of the sixth month, the beginning of summer.
In the midst of spring, lotus blossoms open upon the water’s surface; lychee fruits reflect the crimson of the mountains. The True Person of No Rank meets one everywhere;

yet if you hesitate to grasp it, the clouds and mountains stretch for thousands of miles. When the Master’s life-work was nearing its end, he gathered the two orders of the community and presented them with his final instructions.
He asked for a brush and wrote this verse: Eighty-four years—like a single dream. When the dream breaks, all returns to emptiness; there is not even a trace of anything left behind.
He passed away sitting upright (Gu-feng Xiushi).
Chan Master Jie of the Single Robe at Shuanglin in Wuzhou praised the Venerable Fu with this verse:
Neither Confucian, nor Daoist, nor yet Chan, His makeshift practice is truly pitiable. Leaving his one life unfinished in three ways, To this day, eight hundred...
There were two others: Nian Gufeng (Xiu) and Shisi (the above two).
Chan Master Ge Lu Tan cited a monk’s question to Master Shixi: “What is the Buddha? Shixi replied, “A short man watching a play.
He then offered this verse: “Majestic is the sixteen-foot purple-gold countenance; In the arena of a hundred performances, there is transformative skill. The short man...”
His eyebrows appear arched and prominent; his iron hammer, though without holes, dances in the spring breeze (Rong’an Haishi).

Chan Master Daming Bao of Mazu, of the Caodong school, visited Puzhao Bian and asked: "Regarding that which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations, I request the Master..."
"Pointing directly to the meaning of the Westward Journey," Bian said, "Yesterday someone asked this very same question and was beaten away.
The Master said, "What about today? Bian said, "How can you be so insensitive to pain? The Master bowed. Bian said, "What a pity! The staff is broken.
The Master was so overcome that he broke into a cold sweat; suddenly, he attained a profound realization. He then went to stay at Daming Temple.
In the Hall, a monk asked, "What is it to turn function into position? The Master said, "Exhausting all the strength of the spade, one lays down and rests in the pure breeze.
The monk asked, "What is it to turn position into function? The Master said, "Not dwelling in the shadowless valley, one carries the staff and enters the misty village.
The monk asked, "What is it for function and position to be manifested simultaneously? The Master said, "Holding the sun and moon in the palm of the hand, their radiance moves and shines of itself."
"Without partiality. [A monk] asked, "What is meant by 'merit and position both hidden'? The Master said, "The stone man and the wooden woman invite each other to enter the sea.
