Yi asked, "Fire burning at both ends with smoke at one end. The Master had habitually held a small hand-drum (*taogu*) in his hands;
on one side was written the character "Chù" (矗), and on the other side, the character "Bēn" (犇). Whenever he gave an answer, he would frequently raise and shake it. He passed away in peace.
The pagoda is at Longshen Mountain.
Guangxin of Ehu was the Chan Master Yang’anxin, a native of the Zhu family from Shangrao in the commandery.

While visiting his relatives one day, he happened upon a practitioner discussing the meaning of the "four births. Upon hearing these words, the Master thoroughly realized the great principle that all things and the self are equal.
He went to Taiping in Luoyang to shave his head, then returned south to Jiaoshan to pass the winter solstice.

There, hearing the sound of a boat being pushed through the river, he attained realization. His verse says: "The night is still and the river is vast; The sound of the boat being pushed, *li-li*. I know not where I dwell; Half of my burden has grown light.
He visited Huashan and heard the master’s “one piece of livelihood, not contained within the six” kōan. He harbored doubts about it and applied himself with fierce intensity.
After seven days, his body and mind were liberated. He soon returned to his hometown. While residing at Mount Ling, he drew a great circle on the wall and inscribed it with these words:
"Inscribe within so as not to stain it black; inscribe without so as not to damage its whiteness.
If anyone can provide a commentary for what lies inside and outside this circle, I grant that you may study the Way without doubt. Otherwise, you shall all be nothing but failures."

Later, he resided at Gehu (Goose Lake) Monastery. For ten years, he did not appoint a seat-head (zuo-yuan). When Boshan came to study with him, they reached a mutual accord through the "Mu" (No-Word) koan of Zhaozhou.

Boshan requested to hold that office, and the Master presented him with a verse, saying: "For ten years at Goose Lake, the seat-head position lay vacant; For what reason was it established all at once by a youth?

Two eyebrows, eight strands— Know that Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot stand before them. —Master [Xuedou] (Note: The text provided contains a fragment of a Zen record concerning Xuedou Chongxian and his successor Boshan Shengnian.)
Once, he placed a "lock with no door" in his meditation hall to test those from various quarters. He spoke in verse:
"The lock handed down from ancient times— Rely on the key of your own wisdom to open it. If you lack the method to open the lock, Then even if we meet, there is no need to come.

On the final day of the second month in the Dingmao year of the Wanli era, he ascended the hall to preach the Dharma, prepared a vegetarian feast to bid farewell, and again presented this verse: "Over eighty years of illusion..."
In a dream, an iron ox plowed through the great void; as he was about to depart, he entrusted this one phrase:
"At midnight, the golden sun bears the crimson light. He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Wengu Guangyin of Zhenji Temple in Hangzhou was the son of Zhou [family] from Jiaśan.

His mother dreamed that the deity Xuwǔ (Ursa Major) brandished a sword and led various armored soldiers to protect her gate before he was born. At the age of seven, he would often sit upright with his eyes closed.
His parents sent him to Kaiyuan Temple in Hangzhou for ordination. After his tonsure, the Master returned to visit his kin. His mother admonished him, saying: "The three..."

"Welcome, new bride! You are a Chan practitioner of this world; you must exert yourself in this. The Master would often recount these two lines, which he found inexhaustible for his practice throughout his entire life.
One day, seeing a diagram of the Dharma-realm on the wall, he asked his teacher, "The ten realms arise from the mind."
"Where does the mind go? His teacher was unable to answer. At that time, Master Yifeng was living in a thatched hut at Qingping. The Master went there to consult him.
Yifeng said, "If you wish to understand, you must attain wondrous enlightenment. The Master asked, "How can one attain enlightenment?

Yifeng then instructed him to contemplate the character "Lu" (Exposure) from Yunmen. Upon hearing this, the Master immediately believed it and applied himself to its investigation with such intensity that he forgot both sleep and food.
He then traveled up Mount Shuangjing and built a thatched hut at the foot of Baiyun Peak. There he contemplated the karmic conditions of Master Liang’s study under Mazu;
his doubts remained unresolved. One day, seeing yellow *huangruixiang* flowers, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and said:
"It is indeed space that can preach the sutras; even common bricks and rubble are fit to listen. Previously, I had been twisting my mother-born nose and mistakenly taking a gourd for a melon."
Carrying a pure water jar (*śuci-ghaṭa*), he then went to Yunqi, where he fully obtained the benefit of Master Lian’s teachings. Next, he visited Chan Master Zhuan of Longchi.
At that time, Master Zhuan happened to be warming himself in the sun at the foot of the steps. The Master asked, "Where is the Abbot? Zhuan replied, "By chance, he is not here.
The Master immediately performed a prostration. After the formal greetings were concluded, Zhuan showed the Master a verse he had composed on "Deshan Carrying the Alms Bowl."
He then said, "Try composing a verse on your own. The Master immediately composed this verse: "Is there or is there not that final word?
The father and son of Deshan are too much at odds. Born of the same lineage, yet dying of different lineages— To have lived for three years only increases my regret.
Chuanxi was greatly pleased and said to the Master, "Why do you not take up this matter and join us in mutual chanting and composition? The Master did not consent, and Chuanxi said:
"What more could be desired? The Master replied, "I feel much shame when compared to Yuanwu and Dahui.
Huanglong Chuan sighed and said, "Among the students of today, many have not yet attained realization yet claim they have; how could there be anyone like you who is so self-accepting?
I, this old monk, shall yield a head’s length of ground to you. As he was about to depart, Chuan escorted him to the gate and patted the Master on the back, saying, "Old nephew, I am returning."
[Zhao] Zhen said, "I suspect you are here. The Master said, "Where do you suspect me? [Zhao] Zhen said, "What is the secret transmission of its meaning?
The Master said, "Today I shall not strike Yixing. [Zhao] Zhen laughed loudly. The Master donned his bamboo hat and departed, traveling north to Mount Wutai and later returning to Zhenji.
When the fourfold assembly earnestly requested him to open the hall for formal teaching, the Master resolutely refused and subsequently traveled south to live in seclusion.
When the temple in Jianzhou was being demolished, and upon his return from Min, Magistrate Huang Duobu again made a request [for him to take charge].

The Master said, "I have been a widow for a long time; how could I marry again? Throughout his life, the Master lived with such austerity that he was like a drop of water on a frozen surface; he refused to let his mind wander even for a single thought.
Although he had thoroughly penetrated the Gate of the Patriarchs, he sought to turn back worldly customs and never claimed enlightenment for himself. Thus did he teach.

The Vinaya tradition consists of three schools standing like the legs of a tripod; the Master was able to penetrate their subtle nuances in all of them. From time to time he would expound them for the assembly, and there were none among those who heard him who did not submit with heartfelt conviction.
In the twelfth month of the Bingzi year of the Chongzhen era, he took leave of the assembly and entered parinirvāṇa. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the northern slope of Kongqing.
Heposong Wenfasheng Chan Master, whose pen-name was Xuebo (Snow Cypress), was the son of the Li family of Wujiang.
In his youth, he received the tonsure at Huashan and traveled alone as a wandering monk. He went to visit the Venerable Zibo Ke, who asked him:
"I do not ask about 'one phrase containing the three mysteries'; how about 'one mystery containing the three essentials'? The Master snapped his fingers and said: "It is so."
A dead snake on one’s head—this should bring great joy. He was thus titled "The Zen Tiger," and for a time his reputation was preeminent within the monastic community.
While the Master resided at Yun’an in Mount Tiantong, Xueqiao Xin came to attend upon him.

As the Master sat in the firebox, muttering to himself, Xin immediately leaped into the firebox to sit with him and asked, "What are you muttering about? The Master laughed and said, "You have come from..."
"From where have you come to this Tianmu? Xìn replied, "I have come from the ground where neither yin nor yang exists.
The Master remained silent. Xìn then leaped down into the firebox. ○ Lín Gāoyù went to consult the Master. They happened to meet at the mountain gate.
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? Yù spread his two hands. The Master said, "The Heavenly King’s Hall here has collapsed; do you know it? Yù said:
"Since it is the Hall of the Heavenly Kings, why was it overturned? The Master said, "A thief!
One day the Master said to Yan Tianchi, "Last night Qionglong Mountain nodded its head. I do not know what you, Layman, would say about it.
Do not say that the Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hanging on the eastern wall! If you, Layman, are as free and easy as this, it will not hinder me at all."
The Master Duohuohuo resided at Poshan and appointed Han Yuecang as his head seat (shouzuo).

He frequently spoke of the maladies of Chan in recent times, saying that practitioners often merely calculate and speculate upon public cases (*gong'an*), providing commentaries on causal conditions (*yinyuan*) by polishing the joints and fitting the seams, weighing and measuring them down to the last ounce.
This not only isolates themselves for a thousand lifetimes, but further ensnares countless others. In the seventh month of the third year of the Tianqi era, he was about to pass away.

Ji called his attendant to him and immediately sat in the posture of liberation (*āsana*). His entire body was enshrined for twenty-one days, remaining as solemn and lifelike as if he were still alive.
His worldly age was seventy-two. He was interred in a stupa south of Poshan Temple. Chan Master Muyun Men compiled ten volumes of the Master’s recorded sayings (*yulu*) for circulation;
these were prefaces by the Venerable Xueqiao Xin.
Dacheng Shouchao was a native of Tongzhou. He did not disclose his surname or clan. He once studied under Tiantong Wu, serving as the West Hall Attendant;

however, after a short time, he suddenly abandoned his post, leaving no one able to fathom his intent. At times he walked upon ice during the bitter cold, or ascended mountain peaks in the deep night;
at other times he shaved his head like a layman or dressed in the garb of a commoner. He would speak to himself alone, exclaiming incessantly, or discourse on matters of ghosts and illusions.
Those who heard this were struck with doubt and alarm; when he encountered crowds bowing to him, he looked at them as if they were strangers and would often scold them, saying, "I do not know you.
Yet when Master Linji met Master Yuanlin, who was residing in the staff quarters of Tiantong, he paid him profound respect and veneration.
After a short while, he smashed all the beds and seats at once, throwing them down the steps. The assembly was stunned, not knowing what to make of it.

He rearranged them again, but the Master immediately closed the door and remained silent. When the gruel and rice were brought in through the window, the disciples lined up outside the door, calling his name and prostrating;
the Master would not admit them. Suddenly one day, he departed, and no one knew where he had gone. The fourfold assembly mourned him with deep longing.

Muyun Men established a memorial for his master and propagated his Way. The layman Huang Yuti, alias Jiezi, of Jiangyin, met Feiyin Rong at Jinsu Temple. He recounted his own experiences of having visited Tiantong. Rong asked, "How long did you stay there? The layman replied, "Seven or eight days. Rong said, "Did you grasp the meaning of Tiantong? The layman replied, "I did. Rong said, "Then tell me what that meaning is. The layman was speechless. Rong struck him once with his staff and said, "This is it! The layman suddenly attained great awakening. He then composed a verse: "Before the mountain gate, the path is vast; The spring breeze blows across the river. If one asks where the ancient road leads, One must first pass through the clouds. Rong approved. Later, when the layman was about to depart, Rong asked, "Where are you going? The layman replied, "To see Master Muyun. Rong said, "Very well; go and pay your respects to the Master. The layman arrived at the monastery and went directly to the abbot’s quarters. Muyun asked, "Where have you come from? The layman replied, "From Jinsu. Muyun asked, "Who did you meet there? The layman replied, "I met Master Feiyin. Muyun asked, "What did he say? The layman recounted their conversation. Muyun laughed and said, "He is indeed a man of great capacity. You should go back and ask him again. The layman returned to Jinsu and asked Rong, "Master, what did you say when you were questioned by Muyun? Rong replied, "I told him that the meaning of Tiantong is like this. The layman said, "Master, why did you not tell me so before? Rong said, "Because you had not yet seen Muyun. The layman said, "But I have already seen him. Rong said, "You have only seen his face; you have not yet seen his spirit. The layman was speechless. Rong struck him once with his staff and said, "This is it! The layman immediately attained great awakening. He then composed another verse: "The mountain gate is closed, the path is cut off; The spring breeze blows, the river flows clear. If one asks where the ancient road leads, One must first pass through the clouds. Rong approved. The layman then returned to Muyun and related everything. Muyun said, "You have truly seen my spirit. The layman then bowed and departed. Subsequently, the layman went to visit Master Xueyan. Xueyan asked, "Where have you come from? The layman replied, "From Jinsu. Xueyan asked, "Who did you meet there? The layman replied, "I met Master Feiyin. Xueyan asked, "What did he say? The layman recounted their conversation. Xueyan laughed and said, "He is indeed a man of great capacity. You should go back and ask him again. The layman returned to Jinsu and asked Rong, "Master, what did you say when you were questioned by Xueyan? Rong replied, "I told him that the meaning of Tiantong is like this.

The layman said, "Master, why did you not tell me so before? Rong said, "Because you had not yet seen Xueyan. The layman said, "But I have already seen him. Rong said, "You have only seen his face; you have not yet seen his spirit. The layman was speechless. Rong struck him once with his staff and said, "This is it! The layman immediately attained great awakening. He then composed a final verse: "The mountain gate is closed, the path is cut off; The spring breeze blows, the river flows clear. If one asks where the ancient road leads, One must first pass through the clouds. Rong approved. The layman then returned to Xueyan and related everything. Xueyan said, "You have truly seen my spirit. The layman then bowed and departed. It is said that after this, the layman traveled throughout the land, visiting various masters, and wherever he went, he would invariably quote these three verses. His reputation spread far and wide, and many people came to seek instruction from him. Thus, the lineage of the Dharma was transmitted through these successive encounters, ensuring that the true meaning of the patriarchs was preserved and propagated.
“Is it so? The Master said, “It cannot be. Yunrong asked, “Since it cannot be, have you not missed it? The Master said, “If there were anything to be attained, that would truly be missing it.
Yunrong said, “Today I recognize you, Layman. Thereupon, the Master ceased speaking. The Master had long relied upon Master Wuzhuo and had achieved great penetration.
After Wuzhuo passed away, his fellow disciples requested the Master to compile the collection [of his teachings].

The Recorded Sayings and Correspondence of Master Wuguang circulated throughout the world. Later, when Ding moved [to another location], Master Shi was captured and imprisoned in the Stone City (Shitou Cheng) jail.

There he left an inscription on the portrait of Master Mounong, saying: "Recalling my time at Huangyan, I succeeded to the seat at Tiantong. Occupying the Hall of the Foremost Awakened Ones, I maintained a solitary and eminent style.
Using a wedge to extract a wedge, using poison to counteract poison; the snake swallowed the turtle’s nose, the tiger bit the tiger itself. This is the True Command."
Fully raised up: who would dare meet his blade? His every utterance becomes a verse; through a hundred setbacks, he remains inexhaustible. To Foguo, he is a high official; to Dahui, a vassal.
A guide for the chaff and husks, he has moved back and forth within my ignorant heart. Since the national crisis began, his traces have been here and there:

while you, brother, roamed beyond the heavens, I played within the circle of the prison. In both the mundane and supramundane realms, we are both great heroes. We do not fail our former master, the Old Monk.
Thick and shaggy are his eyebrows, joined in a single tuft; his nostrils are open and his breath flows freely. He is the true lineage of Caoxi and the authentic school of Linji.
This is Old Man Shàng (Shangzuo), also known as Mount Master. On the third day, as he was about to pass away, he again composed a poem on his final moments, saying:
"Through the sword-trees and knife-mountains I stride with arms flung wide; Stretching out my two feet, I rub them myself. The three thousand Sugatas were never Buddhas; A hundred..."
"Ten thousand Pāpīyasins—how could they be demons? Though decrepit, even the heavens may grow drunk. Let them overturn the world; let the waters rise in waves as they please.
Last night I dreamed of the hands of an Asura; alas, what can be done about those twin orbs suddenly leaping up?
Having written this on a single broken fan and sent it to Master Mucun Men, he subsequently passed away while seated within the monastery.
Mingzhou Baiyun Yanxiang Lumen was from Xiangyang; his surname and clan name are unknown. In his youth, he was extensively learned in the scriptural teachings.
When he reached the regions of Hao and Si, the scholar-officials all honored and venerated him, no less than they had for Master Huiyuan of the Lotus Society.
He established two monasteries, Tafei and Huacheng, on the site between Mount Shou and Mount Huo. Later...
When he heard that the Elder Mimi was guiding practitioners at Tiantong, the Master changed his clothes, packed his belongings in a cloth bag, and went directly to the master’s seat.

As soon as Wuyi saw him, they reached a profound accord; he applied sharp, piercing probes until [the Master] cast away all his cherished attachments. Before long, he presented this verse: "Several times I have received blows, most intimate;
The wild mind of kalpas has ceased in this very moment. No need for deliberation or asking 'how'; I see my own nature face-to-face."
He clarified the "Blood-Removing" (Pipo) [method] and attained realization of the seal of approval.

After a long time, when the Elder Mi passed away at Tongxuan, the Master heard that Baiyun was not far away and went there immediately to visit him, saying, "My karmic affinity lies here. A tiger emerged from the forest and crouched before the Master;
the assembly was all struck with alarm. The Master said, "Do not be afraid; this is a deity who protects the Triple Gem. He then established a hermitage there.

The tiger then became his attendant. Everyone said that this was the Chan Master Chang returning once more. County Governor Wei Gong, who had long admired the Master’s character, went to visit him at his hermitage.
Indeed, he saw that the Master’s spiritual practice was refined and strict, and his countenance was dignified and serene.
The tiger served him in an extraordinary manner, saying, "I am as different from Master Pang as heaven is from earth, yet we share the same nature. He then donated funds to redeem [the Master].

The temple was completed; it was the renaissance of Baiyun. On the first day of the twelfth lunar month in the Wuxu year of the Shunzhi era, at the hour of Chén, the Master gathered the assembly and instructed them, saying:
"This monastery shall be established as a monastic center for monks from all directions (śāṇavāsika); do not contravene my wish."
After the cremation, he said, "Grind my bones into powder and scatter them upon East Lake, so that the aquatic creatures may benefit. Do not build a stupa by any means.
Having finished speaking, he wrote a verse and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. That evening, his tiger attendant let out a howl and died three days later.

His disciples enshrined their master’s entire body for three years, during which time his countenance remained unchanged. Later, when they performed the cremation, countless *śarīra* relics were found. The disciples...
He cast half of his bones into the lake to fulfill the late master’s vow; the other half was enshrined in a stupa at the right foot of the mountain.
Qinglin Rujian, a senior monk from the Lin clan of Houguan, resolved to seek the Way at the age of eighteen.

He left the mountains to pay homage to Yunqi Zhuhong and further studied under Master Xiansheng Cheng. Upon gaining realization while contemplating the "Mu" (No-thing) koan, he presented this verse: Zhao...
"Zhou’s dog has no Buddha-nature. [The Master] took off his trousers and used them to cover his face.

"The face was never fully covered; half the body remained exposed, causing people to feel loathing. Cheng patted him and certified him. The Master did not consider himself worthy. Later, he returned to Min to visit his parents.
Upon shaving his head, he again crossed the mountain pass to attend upon Cheng. After a long time, he returned to Gushan and resided at Dong’an. When Bo...
When Master Wuyi of Mount Shan opened the Dharma on this mountain, Xiu had long since devoted his heart to him and subsequently claimed to have received his seal of approval.
From that time forward, he deeply concealed his talents and practiced in secret refinement. At the age of eighty-seven, he manifested nirvana at his former hermitage in Shilin.
After seven days had passed, the cremation was performed. The firelight was golden in color and the fragrance was rich and pervasive. The wooden rosary he had habitually carried did not burn.
Master Yutan Yi was a native of Huguang; his clan name was Ning. At the age of nineteen, he went forth under Zhuan Yu Heng to receive the tonsure. Later...
He attended Zen Master Tiantong Wu for a long time. One day, seeing the Master lifting a stone, Wu suddenly shouted, "Turn that stone over!
At these words, the Master attained realization. Wu deeply approved of this. The following day, he took his leave and retired to a secluded life in a thatched hut.
Later, he resided at Jingjiangdu, where disciples gathered daily; yet the Master remained ultimately unconvinced, muttering to himself incessantly.
The chanting of the *fanbai* did not cease. Whenever anyone came to seek instruction, he would scold them, saying: "Go away and practice meditation!

On the first day of the fifth month of the Renzi year of the Kangxi era, he manifested a slight illness. On the eighth day, he summoned his disciples to enter his room and asked, "Do you know where this old monk is going?
En, the attendant, replied: "The bright moon clearly illuminates the traveler at night. The Master said: "Too cliché."
[The student] spoke. He pressed further, saying, "What is the Master’s meaning? The Master said, "Not born in the year of Ren-yin; not dying in the year of Ren-zi. You speak again.
The student said, "Born indeed in the year of Ren-yin; died indeed in the year of Ren-zi. The Master let out a great shout and said, "How can you defile me so?
The student asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master showed him a verse, which began: "A mere span..."
The journey through the clouds spans ninety provinces; at his heels, he freely clenches and unclenches his fists. Before the gate, the willow trees open their golden eyes;

beyond the railing, the myriad peaks smile and nod their heads. Having finished the verse, he asked, "What time is it? The attendant replied, "It is noon. The Master then requested tea and rinsed his mouth.
He sat in the full lotus posture, tossed his cup, and passed away.
The Grand Historian Jiang Chao, whose secular name was Huchun, was a lay practitioner from Jintan in Jiangnan.
He visited Chan Master Tiezhou Hai at Mount Jinshan and asked, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth all have a time of destruction; tell me, will Mount Jinshan be destroyed or not?
Master Hai extended one leg and said, "If you can utter a turning word here, you shall see the ultimate truth. The layman replied, "I shall offer a turning word."
"Not difficult," [the Master] said. "I only fear that you and the Master will be separated by a single layer.
Haikai said, "Even if you speak thus, how can it suffice? Shishi asked, "And what would you say, Preceptor? Haikai said, "Do not let it pass you by right before your face. Shishi said, "Yes, yes.
He then asked about the kōan concerning the jade belt between Su Dongpo and Chan Master Foyin, requesting the Master to provide a turning word on his behalf. Haikai said, "The Mountain."
The Monk said, "If I were to speak on his behalf, I would have to return the jade belt as well. The Layman asked, "Ultimately, what words must be spoken for them to be in accord?
The Master said, "Do not say that this mountain monk has nothing to say. The Layman said, "I thought there was something else. Haichang said, "..."
"Only today have I finally caught a glimpse of it. One day, Master Shi recounted this to his contemporary, Sun Xiaozhe.
Xiaozhe said, "Why did you not say, 'What kind of words are these? Where does he sit? Master Shi stayed at the garden of the layman Xiaozhe for a long time.
Xiao asked, "I have not seen you practicing Chan lately, Elder. The Master said, "Can Chan be seen? Xiao said, "Try to speak of it.
The Master said, "I suppose there is no need to speak of it. The next day, Xiao said to the Master, "The Record of the Great Compassion Pavilion is yours."
The scholar said, "It is an ancient one. Xiao said, "It is mine; my elder brother forgot it. The scholar nodded his head.
Later, when he entered the capital, he sent a letter saying, "This journey has been truly arduous; I hope you will soon compose a *zhāohún* for me. Xiao replied:

"How could my heart not be moved? What evil is there in the north wind? The scholar requested leave to return home. On his way, he passed through Gaoyou and took his leave of Li Xiaoxiao, saying, "I shall wander aimlessly for the remainder of this life. Xiaoxiao asked, "Where will you go? The scholar replied, "Once I have crossed Mount Lu, I shall reach Mount Emei. Later, he indeed passed away at Fuhu Temple on Mount Emei. As he approached death, he left behind a regulated verse: How could my heart not be moved? What evil is there in the north wind? I bid farewell to my parents; On the road, I pass through Gaoyou. He established himself on Mount E and resided at Mount Wutai, where he widely propagated the teachings and the Vinaya; his spiritual influence resonated far and wide throughout the various regions of Jiangnan.

He studied under Hanshan Deqing, Daguan Zhenke, and Xiaoyan Hongbao; finally, he visited Longchi Shouquan, at which time Miyun Yuanwu had succeeded him on the seat.
He served as an attendant for the longest period of any of the disciples and once made this vow: "Now..."
Sheng did not understand the causal conditions for this great matter; he vowed never to lie down on his mat, sitting upright day and night like Mount Tai.
When Wujue saw that his teacher was practicing in such a manner, one day he asked him, "How long have you been here?"
The Master said, "Three years. Wuzhuo asked, "Where were you three years ago? The Master gave him a slap and said, "Right here.
Wuzhuo said, "This was an event from three years ago; what about the matter of three years ago? The Master slapped him again.
Wuzhuo said, "When one slap does not function as a single slap, what then? The Master said, "Today you have been caught..."
At the Abbot’s single question, he was left with nothing but his mouth hanging on the wall. Wuzhuo asked, "What is the matter of daily life?
The Master replied, "When hungry, eat; when cold, add clothing. He then presented this verse: "A single squeeze and cold sweat flows from my entire body."
